In testimony and perpetual confirmation of this matter, two documents of the same tenor have been drawn up [Col. 1190D]. One shall be held by the Church of Paris, under two seals—namely, those of the abbot and chapter of Saint Geneviève; the other shall be held by the church of the Mount, likewise under two seals—namely, those of the bishop and chapter of Blessed Mary of Paris.

Done in the year of the Incarnate Word 1202, in June.

### Letter of Elias, Abbot of Saint Columba of Sens, and John, Master of the Schools of Orléans, Commissioners of the Apostolic See, concerning Confirmation of the Aforesaid Settlement and Peace

To all Christ’s faithful to whom this present document shall come, ELIAS, abbot of Saint Columba of Sens, and JOHN, master of the schools of Orléans, eternal greeting in the Lord.

Since an apostolic rescript had been issued to us directing us to confirm the settlement made between the venerable men Lord Odo, bishop of Paris, and John, abbot of Saint Geneviève, and their churches [Col. 1191A] and chapters, insofar as it had been made without impropriety and voluntarily accepted by the parties, provided that it did not tend to the prejudice of the Apostolic See, we, having taken the advice of experts, carefully inspected the form of that settlement, authenticated by the seals of both the bishop and abbot and of their chapters. We considered its tenor worthy of insertion word for word in this present document; namely: “The bishop of Paris shall have every right,” etc., as in the preceding document to the end.

Having therefore conducted a full inquiry into the matters which the supreme pontiff commanded us to investigate, we found that this settlement had been made without impropriety and voluntarily accepted by the parties; that the Church of Saint Geneviève had suffered no loss in any respect; and that nothing prejudicial to the Apostolic See had been attempted. Therefore, by apostolic authority, we confirm that same settlement as it is contained in the authentic documents and set forth above.

[Col. 1191B] Done in the year of the Lord 1202.

### Letter Containing the Form of Settlement and Peace between Lord Odo, Bishop, and the Church of Paris on the One Hand, and John, Abbot, and the Church of Saint Geneviève on the Other

[Col. 1192A]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity. Amen.

This is the form of the composition and peace between Lord Odo, bishop, and the Church of Paris on the one part, etc., as in the preceding composition to the end. I, John, abbot of Pontigny, have inspected an authentic document secured with the seals of the abbot of Sainte-Geneviève and of the chapter, in which there was contained word for word the same matter that is set out above. And in testimony of this matter I have caused my seal to be affixed to the present page. I, Girard, abbot of Sacré-Port, of the Cistercian Order, have inspected an authentic document secured with the seals of the abbot of Sainte-Geneviève and of the chapter, in which there was contained word for word the same matter that is set out above. And in testimony of this matter I have caused my seal to be affixed to the present page. I, Sebonius, abbot of Saint-Sulpice, of the Cistercian Order, have inspected an authentic document [Col. 1192B] secured with the seals of the abbot of Sainte-Geneviève and of the chapter, in which there was contained word for word the same matter that is set out above. And in testimony of this matter I have caused my seal to be affixed to the present page.

It seemed appropriate also to add here the following letter of Innocent III, by which, after the report of Elias, abbot of Saint-Columba of Sens, and J., master of the schools at Orléans, whom he had delegated in this case, he confirms this composition, although it was issued in the sixth year of his pontificate. There will also be added the letters of Odo, bishop of Paris, from which it appears that he granted to the dean and chapter of Paris the prebend and vicarage which the abbot and chapter of Sainte-Geneviève had formerly held in the cathedral church of Paris.

[Col. 1191]

[Col. 1191B] INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother the bishop of Paris, and to his beloved sons the abbot of Sainte-Geneviève and their chapters: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Whereas a dispute had long been conducted between you concerning parochial right in the parish of the Mount, concerning the [Note: [Col. 1191D] Sainte-Geneviève des Ardents.] chapel of Sainte-Geneviève situated in the city of Paris, and concerning the procurations which you, brother bishop, demanded in the parochial churches of your diocese belonging to the aforesaid church of Sainte-Geneviève [Col. 1191C] of the Mount; and whereas, after the various labours and many expenses which you had borne on both sides on this account, the dispute had been settled by an amicable composition through the mediation of good men, while preserving the reverence due to the Apostolic See: at your humble request that we might deign to place upon that composition the hand of our confirmation for you and your churches, we instructed by our letters our beloved sons Elias, abbot of Saint-Columba of Sens, and J., master of the schools at Orléans [Note: [Col. 1192D] See above, letter 100.] that, if they should ascertain that the composition had been prudently made without impropriety and voluntarily accepted on both sides, and that it did not redound to the prejudice of the Apostolic See—to which the church of Sainte-Geneviève is known to belong immediately—they should, in our stead, confirm it by apostolic authority; afterward informing us of this by their letters, so that we too might confirm it once we had been more fully instructed by their report.

[Col. 1191D] Accordingly, as sons of obedience, proceeding lawfully in the business entrusted to them, and carefully inspecting the form of that composition and the privileges of the church of Sainte-Geneviève, they found that the composition had been made and accepted on both sides as we stated above; and they took care to confirm it by our authority, as we have seen more fully contained in their letters. Therefore, with equal desire and unanimous will, you humbly petitioned us that we might deign, out of the kindness of the Apostolic See, to place upon the same composition [Col. 1192B] the hand of our confirmation. We therefore, holding as ratified and firm what was done by those delegates according to the form of our mandate, confirm by apostolic authority the aforesaid composition, prudently made without impropriety and voluntarily accepted by you, as is more fully contained in the authentic documents drawn up concerning it. Let no one, therefore, etc.

Given at the Lateran, the seventh day before the Kalends of April, in the sixth year of our pontificate. [Col. 1192C]

ODO, by the grace of God bishop of Paris, to all the faithful of Christ to whom the present document shall come: eternal greeting in the Lord.

We wish it to be known to all that, whereas the venerable men, the abbot and chapter of Sainte-Geneviève, had wholly conveyed and relinquished to us and to our successors, by reason of the composition made between us and them, the prebend and vicarage which they held in the church of Blessed Mary of Paris, we afterward granted and relinquished the said prebend and vicarage to our beloved brothers Hugh, dean, and the chapter of Paris, to be possessed in perpetuity, so that they may dispose of both the prebend and the vicarage as they wish. Nevertheless, the aforesaid chapter shall be bound annually to pay to the same matricular clergy seven Parisian pounds, and, after the resignation or death of Master Albert, sixty shillings of the same currency, in addition to the ten pounds of Parisian money which they granted in perpetuity to the matricular priests newly established by us in our church. [Col. 1192D] Therefore, in order that this gift and grant may remain valid with perpetual force, we have caused the present charter to be secured by the impression of our seal.

Done in the year of the Incarnate Word 1204, in the seventh year of our pontificate.

Above, in letter 128, it is read that William, lord of Montpellier, asked Innocent III to deign to honour with the title of legitimacy the children whom he had begotten by a subsequently introduced woman, and that the example of Philip Augustus, king of the French, had been adduced, whose children begotten by a subsequently introduced woman the same pontiff had restored to legitimate birth. I think I shall do a service agreeable to students of these matters if, taking this opportunity, I publish here Innocent’s letters concerning the legitimization of the king’s offspring, together with what was done among us by the Gallican bishops after those letters of Innocent had been received.

[Col. 1191]

[Col. 1191D] INNOCENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers all archbishops and [Col. 1192D] bishops established throughout the kingdom of France: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1193A] The Apostolic See, which by God’s ordinance is the mother and teacher of all the faithful, in the times of our predecessors, after considering diverse causes, granted dispensations to certain persons born less than legitimately, even to those begotten in adultery; legitimizing them for spiritual acts, it also permitted them to be promoted to the episcopate. Since greater fitness is required in spiritual than in secular matters, there can be no doubt that it is able to legitimize such persons for secular acts, especially at the petition of those who acknowledge among men no superior other than the Roman pontiff possessing such authority.

Therefore, since our dearest son in Christ, Philip, king of the French, apart from his firstborn son, whom he received from his first wife, has no other offspring except a boy and a girl, whom the noblewoman, now deceased, daughter of the noble duke of Merania, bore to him; and since, prudently considering his posterity, he humbly requested [Col. 1193B] that we should provide for their legitimization through the favour of the Apostolic See, strongly maintaining that, after our venerable brother William, archbishop of Reims, cardinal of Santa Sabina and then legate of the Apostolic See, pronounced between him and our dearest daughter Ingeburg, illustrious queen of the French, a sentence of divorce—although that sentence was afterward revoked by the Apostolic See because judicial procedure had not been observed—nevertheless no prohibition against marrying another woman came to him; and that, because of the proofs of affinity produced before the same archbishop, which the king believed to be true, he thought that a matrimonial bond existed between himself and the aforesaid noblewoman, although by our authority he was compelled both to dismiss her and to receive back the said queen:

We, therefore, considering in him the constancy of devotion and purity of faith which he has acquired from his forebears toward the Roman Church as though by a kind of hereditary [Col. 1193C] right, and wishing prudently to provide both for the honour of royal dignity and for the utility and need of the kingdom of France, by the common counsel of our brethren adorn the aforesaid boy and girl, by special grace, with the title of legitimacy, so that no defect of birth may stand in their way; provided, however, that by this no prejudice is generated for the same king or the aforesaid queen in the [Col. 1194A] matrimonial case.

You, therefore, shall yourselves firmly observe what has been established concerning this by our prudent deliberation, and shall cause it to be inviolably observed by others through ecclesiastical censure; and, when requested by the same king, shall solemnly publish it in accordance with the form prescribed above.

Given at Anagni, on the fourth day before the Nones of November, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

Letters of the Gallican bishops.

ODO, by the grace of God humble minister of the Church of Paris, to all, clerics as well as laymen, to whom these present letters shall come: for ever.

Let all of you know that we have seen an authentic document of our most holy father Pope Innocent, in which it is contained that he adorned with the title of legitimacy the son and daughter of our most excellent lord Philip, king of the French, whom he had begotten by Agnes, daughter of the noble duke [Col. 1194B] of Merania, so that no defect arising from birth may stand in their way. We, indeed, as devoted sons of the most holy Roman Church, humbly receiving the apostolic mandate and holding them to be legitimate, by apostolic authority, whose mandate in this matter we have received, have excommunicated, anathematized, and excluded from the thresholds of holy mother Church all those who in any way presume to oppose or derogate in any respect from this apostolic decree.

Done publicly at Sens, in the year of grace 1201, in the month of January.

In the same manner: Peter, archbishop of Sens; Garnerius, bishop of Troyes; Ansellus, bishop of Meaux; William, bishop of Nevers; Hugh, bishop of Orléans; and Hugh, bishop of Auxerre—each separately. Given as above.

In the same manner: William, archbishop of Bourges, and Robert, bishop of Clermont—each separately. Given at Bourges, in the year 1201, in the month of January.

In the same manner: Robert, bishop of Laon; Philip, bishop of Beauvais; Stephen, bishop of Noyon; Lambert, bishop of Thérouanne; and Aymar, bishop of Soissons—each separately. Given at Reims, in the year 1210, in the month of February.

[Note: [Col. 1193] Here, in Baluze’s edition, there is inserted the *Register of Innocent III concerning the affair of the Roman Empire*; we relegate it to the end of the *Regesta*. EDITOR.]

REGESTA, OR LETTERS, OF INNOCENT III.

## BOOK ONE.—First year of the pontificate, A.D. 1198.

pending between the Bishop of Ourense and the Abbot of Cella Nova, whom the bishop claimed to be subject to him by diocesan law. (March 26.) 52

[Col. 1198]

75

LXXXIX.—To Peter, canon of Saint Hilary of Poitiers, nephew of the late Master Aimeric of Partiniac. (April 17.) 77

XC.—To G., archdeacon, cantor, and chancellor of Tournai.—Concerning the conferral of a certain prebend in the Church of Antwerp. (April 13.) 78

CCXXXVIII.—To Everard, bishop of Nitra.—That he should retain property offered to the Church and should not pay tithes from estates which he himself cultivates. (Kalends of June.) 204

CCXXXIX.—To the bishops of Bourges and Palestrina.—One who has been despoiled cannot make payment to others before he has been restored. (V Kalends of June.) 205

CCXL.—To the bishop of Lisieux.—Concerning the duty of an archbishop toward his suffragan and of a suffragan toward his archbishop. 205

CCXLI.—To the bishop of Lisieux. (Kalends of June.) 206

CCXLII.—To the nobleman, son of the duke of Austria.—He commands him to restore to the king of England the money taken by his father. (III Kalends of June.) 206

CCXLIII.—To Garner, prior of Loches.—That he may retain the lease of certain lands, while preserving for the chapter its ancient rent. (II Kalends of June.) 207

CCXLIV.—To the bishop and chapter of Angoulême.—Canons not residing at their church cannot invalidate measures rightly established during their absence. (VIII Ides of June.) 208

CCXLV.—To the archbishop of Canterbury, the bishops of Lincoln and Worcester, and the abbot of Tewkesbury.—That monks expelled from their monastery should be restored to their former condition. (III Nones of June.) 208

CCXLVI.—To the archbishop of Bordeaux and the abbots of Saint Cybard and Nantolien.—The case of P. of Angoulême against Ar. de Mairinac, concerning the archdeaconry of Angoulême, is committed to them. (Nones of June.) 209

CCXLVII.—To the bishop of Nevers and the abbots of Saint Bénigne of Dijon and of La Théologie.—The case of the bishop of Autun against the abbot of Buxeria is committed to them, concerning the will and goods of a deceased man whom the abbot maintained had been a monk. (IV Nones of June.) 210

CCXLVIII.—To the abbot of Saint Eucharius, the dean, and L., canon of Trier.—The case of litigants concerning a prebend in the college of Verdun is committed to them. (VIII Ides of June.) 212

CCXLIX.—To Brother Rainer.—That he should compel the kings of Portugal and Castile to observe the treaty concluded and confirmed by oath. 214

CCL.—To the bishop of Newcastle.—That it is lawful to recover property alienated by predecessors. (Nones of June.) 214

CCLI.—To the archbishop of Esztergom.—The privileges of the Church of Esztergom are confirmed. (II Nones of June.) 215

CCLII.—To Brother John and the other brethren of the house of the Holy Trinity of Cerfroid.—Property given to them, to be devoted to pious uses, is confirmed by apostolic authority. (XVII Kalends of June.) 215

CCLIII.—To the bishop and archdeacon of Zamora, and Didacus, prior of Morerola.—That they should hear the case of the chapter of León against the monastery of Saint Facundus. (II Nones of June.) 216

CCLIV.—To Alfonso, bishop of Ourense.—A certain new statute is confirmed. (VIII Ides of June.) 216

CCLV.—To the bishop of Conversano and the archdeacon of Otranto.—That they should investigate the bishop of Mutila, a squanderer and guilty of other crimes, and restore the archdeacon whom he had despoiled. 216

CCLVI.—To the consuls and people of Benevento.—That the testimony of a single judge is not to be believed in legal cases. (IV Ides of June.) 217

CCLVII.—To the consul-judges and people of Benevento.—He confirms the statute concerning the palace of the judges and notaries. (V Ides of June.) 218

CCLVIII.—To the archbishop and chapter of Benevento.—That they should receive the subdeacon Albert as a canon. (Ides of June.) 218

CCLIX.—To Walter, archbishop of Rouen, and his chapter.—In the repair of a church, the decree of the greater and sounder part prevails. (V Ides of June.) 219

CCLX.—To Walter, archbishop of Rouen.—That he should boldly exercise his jurisdiction and not fear royal threats, trusting in the pope’s support. (III Nones of June.) 219

CCLXI.—To the bishop of Worcester.—Concerning the punishment of simoniacs. (VI Ides of June.) 220

CCLXII.—To the bishop and canons of Huesca.—That a certain forger should be punished. (Kalends of June.) 221

CCLXIII.—To the bishop of Amiens.—That, if the abbot has been admonished and remains negligent, he himself should restore the monastery. (XVII Kalends of June.) 221

[Col. 1204]

CCLXIV.—To Walter, archbishop of Rouen.—That no one can present himself to benefices. (III Ides of June.) 222

CCLXV.—To the same.—All are bound to obey a sentence of interdict pronounced by a bishop. 222

CCLXVI.—To the same.—Of nearly the same purport. 222

CCLXVII.—To the bishop, archdeacon, and sacristan of Maguelonne.—A detailed discussion concerning the archdeaconry of Maguelonne. (VI Ides of June.) 223

CCLXVIII.—To the archbishops of Arles, Aix, and Embrun, and their suffragans.—That they should protect and defend the monastery of Saint Victor of Marseilles. (Ides of June.) 225

CCLXIX.—To the bishop of Várad.—That he should come to the Apostolic See to be absolved. (XVIII Kalends of July.) 226

CCLXX.—To the illustrious king of Hungary.—That he may retain twenty men, who were intending to depart for the Holy Land, in order to preserve the peace of his kingdom. (XVI Kalends of July.) 227

CCLXXI.—To the nobleman Duke A.—Concerning the praises of the kingdom of Hungary, and that he should not make war upon the king. (XVIII Kalends of July.) 227

CCLXXII.—To the bishop of Transylvania.—Privileges granted to him by Gregory are confirmed. (XVII Kalends of July.) 228

CCLXXIII.—To the archbishop of Arles.—Concerning the reform of the monastery of Lérins. (Ides of June.) 229

CCLXXIV.—To the archbishop of Arles.—That monks may be established on the island of Arearum with the bishop’s consent and approval. (XVII Kalends of July.) 230

CCLXXV.—To the archbishop and archdeacon of Narbonne.—That they should revoke proceedings undertaken after an appeal duly lodged, and absolve the excommunicated person. (III Ides of June.) 230

CCLXXVI.—To the chapter of Saint John of Besançon.—That, with the archbishop’s consent, they may establish a new college. (V Ides of June.) 231

CCLXXVII.—To the archbishop of Besançon.—He absolves him from the chapter’s accusation, though a canonical purgation is imposed. (IV Ides of June.) 232

CCLXXVIII.—To the abbots of Cîteaux and Tulle.—That the treasurer of Besançon should be summoned to personal residence. (VI Ides of June.) 233

CCLXXIX.—To the archbishop of Milan.—Papal letters are to be received and executed unless they are found to have been fraudulently obtained. (XIII Kalends of July.) 233

CCLXXX.—To the provost and canons of the Church of Kalocsa.—He confirms their right to receive tithes from certain villages. (Ides of June.) 234

CCLXXXI.—To the archbishop of Kalocsa.—The restoration of the monastery of Saint Stephen is committed to him. 234

CCLXXXII.—To the patriarch of Grado.—That the agreement concluded between the Church of Saint Saviour and the Church of Saint Bartholomew of Venice should be observed. (XIV Kalends of July.) 235

CCLXXXIII.—To Hugh, abbot, and the convent of Saint Zeno of Verona.—By a judgment he decides their case against the Church of Saint Proculus concerning subjection. (XIII Kalends of July.) 237

CCLXXXIV.—To Ralph, abbot of the Church of Saint Osyth at Chich, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.—Concerning confirmation of the order and its privileges, and the rule of life. (Ides of June.) 240

CCLXXXV.—To the bishop of Segovia.—Disregarding the votes of absentees or of those who oppose rashly, the greater and sounder votes of the others are to prevail. (IV Ides of June.) 241

CCLXXXVI.—To the abbot of the monastery of Saint Germanus of Auxerre and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.—Concerning their privileges and their reception under apostolic protection. (A.D. 1198.) 241

CCLXXXVII.—To the bishop of Pamplona.—That during a general interdict he may celebrate with closed doors and without ringing bells. (Ides of June.) 244

CCLXXXVIII.—To the bishop of Reggio.—Concerning the case of the dean of Saint Quentin against his chapter. (X Kalends of July.) 245

CCLXXXIX.—To the archbishop of Reims, cardinal of Santa Sabina, and the bishop of Arras.—Concerning the same matter. 245

CCXC.—To Siffred, provost of Augsburg.—That, for various reasons, he confirms his election. 246

CCXCI.—To the archbishop of Bourges.—That he should investigate the abbot of Stirpense, who has been publicly accused. 249

CCXCII.—To G., bishop of Aquino.—That alienations and sales made by his predecessor should be annulled. (VIII Kalends of July.) 250

CCXCIII.—To B., bishop of Vatia.—A certain constitution concerning the observance of a synod is confirmed. (XII Kalends of July.) 251

CCXCIV.—To Nicholas, bishop of Miletus.—That property alienated by predecessors should be recovered. (VII Kalends of July.) 251

[Col. 1205]

CCXCV.—To the archbishop of Trani and the archdeacon of Brindisi.—The case of his notary Philip against Thomas VI concerning the chantry of Otranto is committed to them. (IX Kalends of July.) 252

CCXCVI.—To the canons of the basilica of the Prince of the Apostles, present and future, canonically appointed in perpetuity.—That he wishes to make richer, in honour of the Apostles, the Church in which he himself had been a canon. (III Ides of March.) 254

CCXCVII.—To the bishop, Gautier, and John, archdeacons of Exeter.—Benefices taken from a madman are ordered to be restored; and one tonsured unwillingly and under compulsion is not to be kept in a monastery against his will. (X Kalends of July.) 255

CCXCVIII.—To the archdeacon of Milan.—That heretics can neither be elected to, nor elect persons to, any dignities. (XVII Kalends of July.) 256

CCXCIX.—To the bishop of Nevers and the abbots of Virziliac and La Macerie.—The case of the abbot of Flavigny against the prior of Semur is committed to them. 257

CCC.—To the archbishop of Magdeburg and his suffragans.—That no injuries should be inflicted upon those labouring for the recovery of the Holy Land. (V Kalends of July.) 261

CCCI.—To the bishop of Lisieux and the abbot of Val-Richer.—The case of the abbot of Conches is committed to them. 261

CCCII.—To the bishop of Syracuse and the abbot of Sambucina.—That they should preach the cross and exhort men to the recovery of the Holy Land. 263

CCCIII.—To the convent of Saint Saviour of Tilesio.—Concerning the election of a worthy and useful abbot. (V Nones of July.) 266

CCCIV.—To the bishop and chapter of Limoges.—That they should receive a certain Master Peter as a canon. (X Kalends of July.) 266

CCCV.—To the bishop and dean of Mâcon.—The greater and sounder part of the chapter is to prevail in making decisions. 267

CCCVI.—To Aymon, dean of Mâcon.—That sacrilegious persons and plunderers of Church property should be restrained. 267

CCCVII.—To the bishop of Mileto.—An abbot is removed because of a serious bodily infirmity. (V Kalends of July.) 268

CCCVIII.—To the archbishop of Sens.—Concerning the penance and absolution of the archdeacon of Lyons. (III Nones of July.) 268

CCCIX.—To the bishop of Padua.—That clerics should surpass in good life and morals the laity whom they excel in rank. (Kalends of July.) 269

CCCX.—To the archbishop of Monreale.—Concerning the absolution of those who lay violent hands upon clerics. (III Nones of July.) 269

CCCXI.—To the abbot and monks of Bourgueil.—Concerning the office of abbot and the restoration of monastic discipline. (Nones of July.) 270

CCCXII.—To the bishop, P. the archdeacon, and the dean of Wirchia of Rennes.—Of the same purport as the preceding. 271

CCCXIII.—To R., archpriest; R., master of the schools; and P. de Vico, canon of Saint Austregisilus of Bourges.—That tithes due to their church should be paid. (Nones of July.) 272

CCCXIV.—To the priest Midran.—The pope states that he confirms the cardinal’s judgment. (VII Ides of July.) 273

CCCXV.—To the archbishop of Milan.—That he should make Bonacosa, a cleric and his messenger, a canon. (VII Ides of July.) 274

CCCXVI.—To Charo, archbishop of Monreale, and his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.—He confirms the privileges granted by his predecessors. (V Kalends of May.) 275

CCCXVII.—To the abbot and convent of Pegau.—Concerning their case against the bishop of Merseburg. (III Ides of July.) 279

CCCXVIII.—To the abbots of Neuburg and the Valley of Saint George, and the provost of Saint Severus of Erfurt.—Of nearly the same purport as the preceding. (XII Kalends of August.) 283

CCCXIX.—To the archbishop, dean, and precentor of Lyons.—The case concerning the archdeaconry of Chalon is committed to them. 283

CCCXX.—To P., bishop of Skálholt, B., bishop of Hólar, and all other prelates and clerics of churches established throughout Iceland.—He informs them of certain grave vices which they should correct throughout Iceland. (III Kalends of August.) 286

CCCXXI.—To the princes and peoples established throughout Iceland.—Of the same purport. 288

CCCXXII.—To the archbishop of Otranto.—That a son born of a woman thought to be a concubine, but later found to be a lawful wife, is legitimate. (III Nones of August.) 288

CCCXXIII.—To the bishops of Huesca and Tarazona.—Concerning a deacon whose friends had murdered an abbot. (II Nones of August.) 289

CCCXXIV.—To the bishop of Arras and the dean of Cambrai.—That they should compel the king of France to restore a dowry to the duke of Lorraine. (VIII Ides of August.) 290

CCCXXV.—To Conrad and Peter, formerly sons of Malabranca.—A girl cannot contract betrothal before her seventh year. 290

CCCXXVI.—To the bishop of Faenza.—He grants permission to transfer to the Church of Pavia. (VI Ides of August.) 291

CCCXXVII.—To Alfonso, bishop of Ourense, and his chapter.—Their statute concerning the number of canons is confirmed. 293

CCCXXVIII.—To R., priest-cardinal of Saints Marcellinus and Peter, and to the abbot and convent of Monte Cassino.—He commends to them the bishop of Saint George, that they may support him generously until he recovers. 293

CCCXXIX.—To the archbishop of Cagliari, the bishop of Sorres, and the archbishop-elect of Torres.—The case of the archbishop of Arborea against his chapter is committed to them. (III Ides of August.) 294

CCCXXX.—To the bishop of Limoges.—That he may freely and boldly correct clerical vices. (III Ides of August.) 297

CCCXXXI.—To Peter, abbot of Prémontré, and the other abbots and canons of the Premonstratensian Order, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.—Concerning their approval, privileges, and manner of life. (VI Kalends of August.) 297

CCCXXXII.—To the dean of Lisbon and the priors of Alcobaça and Saint Mary of Carcadi.—The case of the bishop of Coimbra and the monastery of the Holy Cross is committed to them. (II Ides of August.) 302

CCCXXXIII.—To the archbishop of Arles.—That a mute and deaf person may contract marriage. (Ides of July.) 304

CCCXXXIV.—To the archbishop of Tarentaise, the bishop of Augsburg, and the abbot of Bonmont. (XIV Kalends of August.) 305

CCCXXXVI.—To the archbishop of Narbonne and his suffragans, and likewise to abbots, priors, and other prelates.—He exhorts them to holy war against the Saracens for the recovery of the Holy Land. (XVIII Kalends of September.) 308

CCCXXXVII.—To the bishop and chapter of Treviso.—Concerning the conferral of the provostship of Treviso, which had already devolved to the Apostolic See. (Nones of August.) 313

CCCXXXVIII.—To the archbishop of Siena and P., cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, legate of the Apostolic See.—That a fixed number of canons, secured by oath, should not be increased. (XI Kalends of September.) 313

CCCXXXIX.—To the bishop and canons of Hyporeia.—Concerning the reception of John, the papal subdeacon, to the archdeaconry. (VII Kalends of September.) 315

CCCXL.—To the canons of Borgo San Donnino.—Concerning their privilege and exemption, that they should not be harassed by the bishop of Parma. (VII Kalends of September.) 316

CCCXLI.—To the archbishop of Acerenza.—That ecclesiastical property should not be administered by laymen, but that monasteries once built should be consecrated by bishops. (VI Kalends of September.) 316

CCCXLII.—To the prior of the Church of Saint Nicholas of Monte, situated near Narni.—Concerning their privileges and immunity. (VI Kalends of September.) 317

CCCXLIII.—To the bishop of Lydda.—That he should arm the Sicilian for holy war to recover the Holy Land. (III Kalends of September.) 317

CCCXLIV.—To the same.—Of precisely the same purport. (Kalends of September.) 318

CCCXLVII.—To the same.—That he should compel the king of France, by ecclesiastical censures, to receive back his wife. 320

CCCXLVIII.—To Ph., illustrious king of the Franks.—That he should receive back the queen, his wife, and keep peace with the king of England. 321

CCCXLIX.—To the archdeacon, archpriest, and canons of Milan.—The ways in which the crime of forgery may be committed in connection with apostolic bulls. (II Nones of September.) 322

CCCL.—To the priors of Faversham, Saint Augustine, and Saint George, situated in the diocese of Canterbury.—That persons who have duly appealed to the Apostolic See should not be obstructed. (IV Nones of September.) 324

CCCLI.—To the priors of Saint Augustine and Saint George of Canterbury.—Of the same purport. (III Ides of September.) 324

CCCLII.—To the bishop of Ariano.—Concerning the election and confirmation of the abbot of Benevento. (XVIII Kalends of October.) 325

CCCLIII.—To the illustrious emperor of Constantinople.—That he should stoutly resist the Saracens and compel the Greek Church to return to the Latin Church as to its mother. 325

CCCLV.—To the illustrious king of the Franks.—That he should make peace with the king of England and wage holy war against the Saracens. 329

CCCLVI.—To the podestà and people of Spoleto, the barons, nobles, and all our faithful subjects established in the diocese of Spoleto.—That they should obey the cardinal appointed to the magistracy by the Roman pontiff. 331

CCCLIX.—To Octavian, bishop of Ostia, our vicar.—Concerning the consecration of altars, by command of the Apostle Peter. 336

CCCLX.—To the consuls of Milan.—That Passaguerra was justly excommunicated. 337

CCCLXI.—To our faithful subjects, the men of Montefiascone.—Concerning the surrender of a castle and certain goods, that they may fight for the Church. 339

CCCLXII.—To the abbot of Saint Proculus and Master Lafranc, canon of Bologna.—Concerning a matrimonial case. (XV Kalends of October.) 340

CCCLXIII.—To the bishop of Limoges and the abbot of Saint Cybard of Angoulême.—That property taken from the Church and revenues withheld should be restored. (II Ides of August.) 341

CCCLXIV.—To the archbishops of Armagh and Cashel and the bishop of Laon.—That they should proceed in the case against the bishop-elect of Ross. (XV Kalends of October.) 342

CCCLXV.—To the men of Saint Agatha.—Their reasonable and ancient customs are confirmed. (XI Kalends of October.) 344

CCCLXVI.—To the chapter, clergy, and people both of the city and diocese of Lethglenn.—Concerning the election and consecration of the bishop of Lethgien. 344

CCCLXVII.—To the noble count of Mauritania.—That he should not violate ecclesiastical liberty and privileges. (XIV Kalends of October.) 345

CCCLXVIII.—To the archbishop of Milan.—Concerning the collection of the Milanese chancery. (IX Kalends of October.) 346

CCCLXIX.—To the consuls and people of Castello, the noblemen, and others established throughout the diocese of Castello.—That they should take an oath of fidelity to the pope. 352

CCCLXX.—To Hubert, archbishop of Canterbury.—Concerning the recovery of Church property. (XIV Kalends of October.) 352

CCCLXXI.—To Hubert, archbishop of Canterbury.—He confirms a certain decree of the king of England. (XV Kalends of October.) 352

CCCLXXII.—To Absalon, archbishop of Lund.—Concerning the gift of certain goods, especially the castle of Hasi. (X Kalends of October.) 353

CCCLXXIII.—To Peter, bishop of Aarhus.—He confirms the statute establishing six prebends. (XI Kalends of October.) 354

CCCLXXV.—To John, podestà, and the people of Perugia.—He receives the Perugians into his protection, while preserving their ancient privileges. (VI Nones of October.) 355

CCCLXXVII.—To the bishop of Narni.—That he should hear the case of the abbot of Ferentillo. (III Nones of October.) 356

CCCLXXVIII.—To the noblemen Uguit and Guido Marchioni, our faithful subjects.—He receives them and their subjects under apostolic protection. 359

CCCLXXIX.—To the nobleman of Spalatro.—Permission is granted him to enter a monastery and the Order of Saint Benedict. (IV Nones of October.) 359

[Col. 1208]

CCCLXXX.—To the bishop of Lincoln and the dean of Huntingdon.—That they should pronounce a divorce between P. and T., since spiritual kinship has arisen between them. (VIII Ides of October.) 360

CCCLXXXI.—To the archbishop of Nidaros.—A reply is given to his consultations. (VI Ides of October.) 360

CCCLXXXII.—To the archbishop of Nidaros, all bishops, and other prelates of churches established in Norway and remaining in the communion of the faithful.—Concerning the restraint of the tyrant who was cruelly tormenting them. (II Nones of October.) 362

CCCLXXXIII.—To the illustrious king of the Danes.—Of the same purport. 363

CCCLXXXIII.—To the archbishop of Nidaros.—That he should depose the bishop of Bergen, a supporter of the tyrant. 363

CCCLXXXV.—To the bishop of Verona, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church.—Concerning the deposition from holy orders of a homicide. (VII Ides of October.) 364

CCCLXXXVI.—To R., priest-cardinal of the title of Saints Marcellinus and Peter, abbot of the monastery of Monte Cassino.—That he should reform both his own lax morals and those of his monastery. (XVII Kalends of November.) 365

CCCLXXXVII.—To the noblemen Henry, Leonard, and Mark Mauricen, citizens of Venice.—That they should revoke a certain severe decree issued against Andrew, a jurist. (IV Ides of October.) 367

CCCLXXXVIII.—To the archbishops of Esztergom and Kalocsa and their suffragans.—That the liberty and immunity of churches should be preserved. (XII Kalends of November.) 368

CCCLXXXIX.—To Master Apollinaris, cleric of our venerable brother the archbishop of Esztergom.—A person is not released by appeal from an oath that he will defend the rights of the Church. 568

CCCXC.—Letter of the archbishop of Reggio to the lord pope.—That a case jointly delegated to three persons could not rightly be decided by two, with the third excluded. (The twenty-fifth day of August.) 369

CCCXCI.—Letter of the archbishop and convent of Monreale to the lord pope.—Concerning the same matter. 370

CCCXCII.—To the archbishop of Reggio and the bishop of Cefalù.—The case of which the two preceding letters speak is committed to them. (Kalends of November.) 371

CCCXCIII.—To the bishop, consuls, and people of Parma.—Concerning money violently taken from a cardinal while travelling. (X Kalends of November.) 372

CCCXCIV.—To the bishop of the city of Castello.—He prescribes the rule to be observed concerning the burial of the dead, between the bishop and the Cistercians. (XII Kalends of November.) 372

CCCXCV.—To Brother Rainer.—Authority is given him to reform churches through which he passes. (III Kalends of November.) 373

CCCXCVI.—To the archbishop of Aix.—That he should receive the resignation of the bishop of Fréjus and ensure that another suitable bishop is elected. 374

CCCXCVII.—To the nobleman R., count of Toulouse.—That he should take up arms against the pagans. (II Nones of November.) 374

CCCXCVIII.—To Brother Fulk.—That, with other pious men, he should set out for the holy warfare. (Nones of November.) 375

CCCXCIX.—To archbishops, bishops, and other prelates of churches established in the kingdom of France.—That usurers should be punished notwithstanding any appeal. (V Kalends of November.) 376

CD.—To the archbishop of Siponto.—Concerning the conversion of a collegiate church into a monastery of monks. (VII Ides of November.) 376

CDI.—To the nobleman Acerbo, prior, and the other rulers of Tuscany and the Duchy.—That they should persist in devotion to the Church; its favour and protection are promised them. (III Kalends of November.) 377

CDIII.—To the archpriest and clerics of the Church of Borgo.—That they should again obey the bishop of Parma, as one absolved and reconciled. (II Ides of November.) 378

CDVI.—To the bishop and the provosts of Saint Michael and Saint Epiphanius of Pavia.—That they should investigate the property and number of canons, and the collation of B. (VI Kalends of November.) 382

CDVII.—To the nobleman W., count of Forcalquier.—That he should depart for holy war with the other Christian princes. 384

[Col. 1209]

CDVIII.—To the nobleman R. de Agout.—That he should invite the count of Forcalquier to the holy war. 385

CDIX.—To the archbishop of Pisa, the bishop of Urbino, and the priors of Camaldoli and Saint Fridianus.—That the pope intends to devote money collected not to his own uses but to the public good. (XIII Kalends of December.) 386

CDXII.—To the archbishops, bishops, and other prelates of churches, and all the clergy established in Sicily.—Of the same purport as the preceding letter. 389

CDXIV.—To An., archbishop of Naples.—That plurality of benefices should be restricted. (Ides of November.) 392

CDXV.—To An., archbishop of Naples.—That an oath contrary to good morals and law is not binding. (XVIII Kalends of December.) 392

CDXVI.—To abbots, abbesses, and other prelates of churches subject to the Church of Naples.—That Church property and possessions should not be alienated. (XVII Kalends of December.) 393

CDXVII.—To An., archbishop of Naples.—That, because of debts, it is lawful to sell certain property of the Church. (Ides of November.) 393

CDXVIII.—To the dean and chapter of Blessed Hilary of Poitiers.—That they should confer a prebend upon Peter, nephew of Aimeric de Parthenay. (II Ides of November.) 394

CDXIX.—To Absalon, archbishop of Lund, and his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.—Concerning the primacy of the archbishop of Lund. (IX Kalends of December.) 395

CDXX.—To the provost of Serand and all prelates of churches established in Jutland.—Concerning certain grave abuses to be corrected without delay. (Ides of November.) 396

CDXXI.—To Absalon, archbishop of Lund. 398

CDXXII.—To A., archbishop of Lund, and his chapter.—Concerning the manner of giving Church property in Denmark. (XVI Kalends of December.) 398

CDXXIII.—To S., provost of Strand.—He confirms the provostship conferred upon him. (XVI Kalends of December.) 399

CDXXIV.—To Absalon, archbishop of Lund.—That churches taken from the provost of Strand should be restored. (VIII Kalends of December.) 399

CDXXV.—To Joffrid, abbot of the monastery of Sore, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.—He confirms their privileges and gifts. (IX Kalends of December.) 399

CDXXVI.—To the consuls and people of Todi.—He receives them under apostolic protection and confirms their former privileges. 400

CDXXVII.—To the abbot and monks of Montis Sacri.—He settles a long-standing dispute concerning superiority and obedience between the monasteries of Montis Sacri and Calano. (IV Ides of November.) 401

CDXXVIII.—To the chapter of Cambrai.—That an investigation and decision concerning the faults of their bishop-elect should be made before they elect another. 405

CDXXIX.—To the bishop of Paris.—An inquiry and examination concerning the life and conduct of the bishop-elect of Cambrai is committed to him. 405

CDXXX.—To the bishop of Arras.—That he himself should pronounce judgment concerning the life and conduct of the bishop-elect of Cambrai. 406

CDXXXI.—To the abbot and convent of Compiègne.—The bishop of Senlis is appointed their judge in all their cases. (II Kalends of December.) 406

CDXXXII.—To Hubert, archbishop of Canterbury.—That he should cease and desist from constructing the chapel of Lamhec. (XII Kalends of December.) 407

CDXXXIII.—To the suffragans of the Church of Canterbury.—That they should not obey their archbishop, who scorns to obey the supreme pontiff. (XII Kalends of December.) 413

CDXXXIV.—To the bishops of Lincoln and Ely and the abbot of Saint Edmund.—That they should restore to the monks, with the fruits received, property taken by the archbishop of Canterbury. (XI Kalends of December.) 414

CDXXXV.—To Richard, illustrious king of England.—That the king should not obstruct this restitution to the monks. (XII Kalends of December.) 415

[Col. 1210]

CDXXXVI.—To the prior and convent of Canterbury.—A letter of consolation in the case concerning the archbishop and the monks. (XII Kalends of December.) 416

CDXXXVII.—To Aimeric, illustrious king, and A., queen of Jerusalem.—He receives the kingdom of Jerusalem under apostolic protection. (IV Nones of December.) 417

CDXXXVIII.—To the count of Tripoli.—That he should assist the king of Cyprus, fighting against the Saracens, in preserving and governing the kingdom. 417

CDXXXIX.—To all inhabitants of the province of Jerusalem.—That those deprived of the fulfilment of a vow to go to Jerusalem should nevertheless be bound to contribute some money to the holy war. 418

CDXL.—To the bishop of Acre.—That the number of canons should not be increased beyond the means available. 419

CDXLI.—To Sancho, illustrious king of Portugal.—He, his kingdom, and all his goods are received under the protection of the Apostolic See. 419

CDXLII.—To the dean and chapter of Avranches.—That acts undertaken while litigation and an appeal are pending should be revoked. (VII Ides of December.) 419

CDXLIII.—To the archbishop of Rouen.—Of the same purport. (Nones of December.) 420

CDXLIV.—To the bishop of Uppsala.—Concerning illegitimate persons, who are not to be ordained or elected to dignities. (Nones of December.) 420

CDXLV.—To the bishop of Périgueux.—Authority is given him to visit monasteries, establish churches, and correct abuses. 421

CDXLVI.—To the same.—That wandering monks should be confined in monasteries. (VI Nones of December.) 422

CDXLVII.—To the archbishop of Tours.—That no one except the Roman pontiff may transfer bishops to another church. (III Nones of December.) 422

CDXLVIII.—To the king of Portugal.—That he should pay the tribute promised to the Roman Church. (V Ides of December.) 424

CDXLIX.—To Brother Rainer.—That he should exhort the king of Portugal to pay the annual tribute owed to the Roman Church. 425

CDL.—To the archbishop of Lund.—That collectors of alms should be appointed who are pious and good, while those who offended the people are rejected. 425

CDLI.—To the canons of Novara.—He states that he has confirmed the sentence delivered in their favour against Albert Siccus. (VI Ides of December.) 426

CDLII.—To the bishop of Urgell.—He approves the resignation of the bishopric. 427

CDLIII.—To the chapter of Urgell.—That it should appoint a new bishop over its church. 428

CDLIV.—To the archbishop of Tarragona.—That he should ensure that the canons of Urgell elect some worthy man as bishop. 429

CDLV.—To the archbishop of Pisa.—Concerning the year of probation for monks and the extent to which married persons may be received into monasteries. (IX Kalends of December.) 429

CDLVI.—To the archbishop of Siponto.—Concerning the punishment of those who use false letters. 430

CDLVII.—To the abbot and convent of Saint Edmund.—Concerning the consecration of their church. (Kalends of December.) 431
CDLVIII.---To the clerics of St. Paul of Castro Cervario.---He confirms the judgment rendered in their favor concerning the right of a baptismal font. (5 Kalends of December.) 432

CDLIX.---To the prior and convent of the church of Durham.---That in more important matters they must always seek the abbot’s consent. (6 Ides of December.) 432

CDLX.---To Philip, bishop of Durham.---At what time benefices are to be conferred, and when they devolve upon a superior. 433

CDLXI.---To the bishop of Cesena.---Concerning the relaxation of an interdict. (Ides of December.) 433

CDLXII.---To Rad[ulf], bishop of Périgueux.---That laypersons may not exact tithes from clerics. (18 Kalends of January.) 433

CDLXIII.---To the chapter of Arles.---Certain statutes concerning their manner of life are sent. (4 Ides of December.) 434

CDLXIV.---To the archbishop of Arles.---That he restore the abbot of St. Gervasius to obedience and to the discharge of his office. (Nones of December.) 435

CDLXV.---To Richard, abbot, and the chapter of Compiègne.---Their jurisdiction and privileges are confirmed. (18 Kalends of January.) 435

CDLXVI.---To the suffragans of the church of Arles.---That they obey their archbishop. (4 Ides of December.) 435

CDLXVII.---To the archbishop and chapter of Arles.---That no one be received as a canon in the church of Arles unless he is willing to profess the order of the canons of St. Augustine. [Col. 1211] (Nones of December.) 436

CDLXVIII.---To the bishop of Cenad.---Concerning the precautionary absolution of sick excommunicates until they recover. (17 Kalends of January.) 436

CDLXIX.---To the same.---That clerics constituted in major orders cast off women whom they have taken. 436

CDLXX.---To the bishop of Durham.---The establishment of prebends made in his church is confirmed. 437

CDLXXI.---To the archbishop of Arles.---Concerning the avoidance of plurality of benefices. (4 Ides of December.) 437

CDLXXII.---To the archbishop and chapter of Arles.---That no provost may contract a loan or stand surety without the chapter’s consent. 438

CDLXXIII.---To the archbishop and chapter of Arles.---That the provost render an account of receipts and expenditures. 438

CDLXXIV.---To the archbishop of Arles.---That he may make arrangements concerning ecclesiastical dignities (personatus) according to his will. 439

CDLXXV.---To the provost of St. John of the Cemetery, and his brethren, both present and those to be canonically appointed in the future, in perpetuity.---He receives them under apostolic protection. (18 Kalends of January.) 439

CDLXXVI.---To the archbishop of Arles.---That he restore the monastery of St. Gervasius. (4 Ides of December.) 440

CDLXXVII.---To the abbot of Aurea Vallis, the archdeacon of Poitiers, and Master G., dean of Asianus.---That they defend the pope’s nominees in possession of their benefices, unless the statute fixing a definite number of canons stands in the way. (14 Kalends of January.) 440

CDLXXVIII.---To the dean and chapter of York.---That possession of the prebend and archdeaconry be delivered to Master Peter of Corbeil. (14 Kalends of January.) 442

CDLXXIX.---To the bishop of Ely.---Of the same purport. 443

CDLXXX.---To Richard, illustrious king of England.---Of the same purport. 443

CDLXXXI.---To John, master, and the brethren of the Holy Trinity.---A rule according to which they are to live is granted to them. (16 Kalends of January.) 444

CDLXXXII.---To G., provost of Albi.---He is given authority to confer the custody of Albi. (12 Kalends of January.) 449

CDLXXXIII.---To the bishop of Poitiers.---That he visit and reform the monasteries throughout his diocese. 449

CDLXXXIV.---To Fulk, abbot of the monastery of St. Peter of Corbie, and his brethren in perpetuity.---He receives them under protection and leaves them precepts concerning excellence of life and conduct. (15 Kalends of January.) 450

CDLXXXV.---To R., illustrious king of England.---That he not oppress the monks of Canterbury contrary to right, to the matter already adjudged, and to the authority of the Roman pontiff. (11 Kalends of January.) 451

CDLXXXVI.---To the archbishop of Rouen and the bishop of Ely.---That they present the pontiff’s letters to the king of England, explain them, and commend the monks’ cause. 453

CDLXXXVII.---To Aimery, illustrious king of Jerusalem.---He exhorts him to piety and moderation and promises him his assistance. (12 Kalends of January.) 454

CDLXXXVIII.---To the bishop of Noyon, and the abbots of St. Medard of Soissons and of Compiègne.---That they pursue the wrongs done to the monastery of Corbie and defend its privileges. 455

CDLXXXIX.---To the bishop and chapter of Tournai.---That they refrain from inflicting injuries upon the said monastery. 455

CDXC.---To Maurice, bishop of Nantes.---He transfers him to the church of Poitiers. 456

CDXCI.---To the archbishop of Bordeaux.---Concerning the same matter. 457

CDXCII.---To the dean and chapter of Poitiers.---Of the same purport. 457

CDXCIII.---To abbots and priors, provosts and other prelates of churches, and to all clerics subject under diocesan law to the church of Poitiers.---That they obey their bishop. 457

CDXCIV.---To the archbishop of Narbonne and Brother Rainer.---He approves the resignation of the bishop of Carcassonne. (10 Kalends of January.) 457

CDXCV.---To the archbishop and dean of Sens.---That they defend the church of St. Martin of Tours from injuries. 458

CDXCVI.---To the bishops of Poitiers and Le Mans, and the abbot of La Fontaine.---Of the same purport. 459

CDXCVII.---To the bishop of Coventry.---Concerning the punishment of simoniacs. 459

CDXCVIII.---Letter of Guy, count of Auvergne, to the lord pope.---He gives a castle to the Roman Church and commends his brother’s cause to the pontiff. 460

CDXCIX.---To the archbishop of Kalocsa.---Concerning the reform of the monastery of St. Stephen of Keu. (11 Kalends of January.) 460

[Col. 1212]

D.---To the illustrious king of Hungary.---That he compel the Slavs to pay tithes. 461

DI.---To the abbot and convent of St. Peter of Chartres.---Ecclesiastical benefices are not to be promised to anyone before they fall vacant. (3 Kalends of January.) 461

DII.---To the bishop of Tripoli.---He transfers him to the church of Tripoli. (2 Kalends of January.) 462

DIII.---To the patriarch of Antioch.---Of almost the same purport. 464

DIV.---To the bishop of Langres.---He suspends him from office until he answer his chapter concerning the dissipation of the Church’s goods. 464

DV.---To the patriarch of Jerusalem and the canons of the Lord’s Sepulchre.---He exhorts the patriarch of Jerusalem either to satisfy the patriarch of Antioch concerning certain complaints or to pursue the case before the Roman pontiff. (3 Nones of January.) 466

DVI.---To the brethren of the Order of the Temple.---By apostolic authority he confirms the purchase of certain goods. (4 Nones of January.) 467

DVII.---To the commander and brethren of the house of the Order of the Temple situated near Montpellier.---He confirms an agreement formerly made between them and the provost and chapter of Maguelone. (2 Kalends of January.) 467

DVIII.---To the bishop of Syracuse and the abbot of Sambucina.---Concerning aid for the Holy Land. (Nones of January.) 470

DIX.---To the bishop of Syracuse.---That he endeavor to extirpate the heresies which are springing up. 471

DX.---To S., archbishop of Kalocsa, V., bishop of Gevri[?], and D., bishop of Zagreb.---The elections of the archbishops of Otranto and Split are annulled. (3 Kalends of January.) 472

DXI.---To the archbishops, bishops, and other prelates of churches established in Hungary.---That no one lightly pronounce a sentence of excommunication against the counselors of the king of Hungary. (6 Ides of January.) 473

DXII.---To the patriarch of Antioch.---Concerning the preservation of ecclesiastical liberty, and that exactions and tallages not be imposed upon the Church by laypersons. (Nones of January.) 474

DXIII.---To the archbishop of Tyre.---That witnesses produced to prove an exception be compelled to give testimony in the principal case. (4 Nones of January.) 474

DXIV.---To the archbishop and chapter of Tyre.---That unbelievers joined in a prohibited degree not be separated after baptism. (3 Kalends of January.) 475

DXV.---To the archbishop of Tyre.---That patriarchs and primates ought not to judge, at first instance, subjects of archbishops and bishops. (Nones of January.) 475

DXVI.---To the bishop of Sidon, and the bishops of Beirut and Byblos.---Concerning the payment of tithes. (10 Kalends of January.) 476

DXVII.---To the bishop of Acre.---That one who has professed a religious order be compelled to enter and observe it. 476

DXVIII.---To the patriarch of Jerusalem.---He piously admonishes him concerning his office and declares that, because of his offenses, he will proceed against him according to law. 477

DXIX.---To Fulk, abbot of Corbie.---The use of a ring is granted to him. (3 Kalends of January.) 478

DXX.---To G., bishop of Coventry.---That he recover what has been alienated by his predecessors. (6 Ides of January.) 478

DXXI.---To the same.---That, when patrons disagree in presenting a suitable cleric, the bishop appoint a vicar while the suit is pending. (3 Ides of January.) 478

DXXII.---To the archbishop of Arles.---He is charged to inquire into the situation of the bishop of Riez, who wished to resign his bishopric. 479

DXXIII.---To the archbishop of Besançon and his suffragans.---That no one be elected abbot of Luxeuil unless he is a monk of that monastery. (3 Ides of January.) 480

DXXIV.---To the abbot of Flora.---That a profession made without the habit is binding. 480

DXXV.---To our chaplain and subdeacon, legates of the Apostolic See.---He makes them legates to the king of Dalmatia. (4 Ides of January.) 480

DXXVI.---To Vulcan, illustrious king of Dalmatia and Dioclea.---That he receive the apostolic legates reverently and permit them to carry out their office. 481

DXXVII.---To the archbishop of Dioclea.---Of the same purport. 482

DXXVIII.---To all prelates and clerics throughout Dalmatia and Dioclea.---Of the same purport. 482

DXXIX.---To the bishop and chapter of Tripoli.---That they confer upon Raymond the first canonry and prebend to become vacant. (2 Kalends of January.) 482

DXXX.---To all the clergy and people of Cremona.---Concerning the life, miracles, and canonization of St. Homobonus. (2 Ides of January.) 483

DXXXI.---To the archbishop of Siponto.---One who unknowingly possesses forged letters is deserving of pardon. [Col. 1213] (19 Kalends of February.) 485

DXXXII.---To the dean and chapter of Angers.---By right, the translation of bishops pertains to the Roman pontiff alone. (12 Kalends of February.) 486

DXXXIII.---To Montanarius, our subdeacon.---He confirms to him the priory of St. Savin, to which he had been elected. (10 Kalends of February.) 489

DXXXIV.---To Peter, bishop of Coimbra.---He confirms to him those things which his predecessors had hitherto possessed lawfully. (7 Kalends of January.) 490

DXXXV.---To J., chaplain, and S., subdeacon, our household members and legates of the Apostolic See.---The pallium is granted only to metropolitans. (7 Kalends of February.) 490

DXXXVI.---To the archpriest and canons of the basilica of the Prince of the Apostles.---He declares his goodwill and generosity toward them. (15 Kalends of February.) 490

DXXXVII.---To the bishop of Faro.---That he come to Rome with several canons to state the cause of his translation. (3 Nones of December.) 492

DXXXVIII.---To the canons of Zadar.---Of the same purport. 492

DXXXIX.---To the doge and people of Venice.---That they not furnish arms and assistance to the Saracens under the pretext of trade. 493

DXL.---To the bishop of Gevri[?] and the abbot of Boccan[?].---Concerning the punishment of those who commit forgery. (3 Kalends of February.) 493

DXLI.---To P. of Castronovo, archdeacon of Maguelone.---He confirms the archdeaconry to him. (4 Kalends of February.) 494

DXLII.---To the prior and brethren of Grandmont.---He exhorts them to concord and mutual charity. (3 Kalends of February.) 496

DXLIII.---To the bishop of Constance.---Unless an appeal is lodged within ten days, a judgment passes into a matter adjudged. (3 Ides of January.) 497

DXLIV.---To the bishops of Vác and Cenad, and the abbot of Sziric[?].---He commits to them the examination of a controversy between a bishop and an abbot. (3 Kalends of February.) 497

DXLV.---To the canons of St. Lawrence of Spello.---He confirms the cardinal’s judgment concerning the priory of St. Lawrence. (Kalends of February.) 499

DXLVI.---To the archbishop of Esztergom and the bishops of Pécs and Cenad.---That they investigate the accusation of the chapter of Várad against its bishop. (3 Kalends of February.) 500

DXLVII.---To the abbot of the monastery of Francae Vallis and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.---Concerning confirmation of privileges and possessions. (Kalends of February.) 501

DXLVIII.---To the prioress of the monastery of Courte-Rive and her sisters, both present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.---On the same subject. (3 Kalends of February.) 502

DXLIX.---To Henry, illustrious king of Hungary.---That witnesses examined concerning a certain forgery not be hindered from speaking the truth. (2 Nones of February.) 502

DL.---To the bishops of Lincoln and Winchester, and the abbot of St. Edmund.---That they examine the cause of the bishop of Coventry and the monastery. (3 Nones of February.) 503

DLI.---To Gaudemar, abbot of the monastery of Boscaudon, and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.---Concerning confirmation of privileges. (3 Nones of February.) 504

DLII.---To John, minister of the house of the Holy Trinity of Cervi Frigidi, and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.---He receives them and their house under apostolic protection. (3 Nones of February.) 504

DLIII.---To the bishop and Master P. of Corbeil, canon of Paris.---That they hear the controversy of the chapter of Langres against its bishop. (4 Ides of February.) 505

DLIV.---To the bishop of Coimbra and the other bishops established in the kingdom of Portugal.---He explains the difference between a general and a particular interdict. (7 Ides of February.) 506

DLV.---To the archbishop and chapter of Pisa.---That they exhort their citizens to maintain the peace and concord maintained by the other estates of Tuscany. 507

DLVI.---To the illustrious king of Navarre.---That an oath entered into rashly and dishonorably need not be kept. (3 Ides of February.) 509

DLVII.---To the archbishops of Palermo, Reggio, Capua, and Monreale, and the bishop of Troia, members of the royal household.---That they send without delay the money necessary against the enemies of the kingdom. (8 Kalends of February.) 510

DLVIII.---To the clergy, barons, judges, knights, and all the people of Capua.---That they fight bravely for their country against its enemies. [Col. 1214] 513

DLIX.---To the archbishops, bishops, abbots, priors, and all clergy established throughout Calabria and Apulia.---Of almost the same purport as the preceding letter. 514

DLX.---To the counts, barons, citizens, and all people established in Apulia and Calabria.---Of the same purport. 516

DLXI.---To the archbishops, bishops, and all prelates of churches established in Sicily.---On the same matter. 517

DLXII.---To G., cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Portico, legate of the Apostolic See.---He entrusts to him the guardianship of the underage king and of the kingdom of Sicily. 518

DLXIII.---To the nobleman L. of Aquila, count of Fondi.---That he obey the apostolic legates and give them counsel and assistance. 518

DLXIV.---To the archbishops of Palermo, Capua, Reggio, and Monreale, and the bishop of Troia.---Of the same purport. 519

DLXV.---To the illustrious king of Sicily.---Words of consolation upon the death of his father and mother. 520

DLXVI.---To the archbishop of Palermo.---He entrusts to him the care and restoration of the monastery of Palermo. (6 Ides of February.) 521

DLXVII.---To the master and brethren of the Hospital of Jerusalem.---That they pursue their cause against the brethren of the Order of the Temple by law, not by force. 521

DLXVIII.---To the primicerius and clergy of Milan.---That provision for apostolic legates and nuncios is due from all according to a just measure. (12 Kalends of March.) 523

DLXIX.---To the abbot of Cerreto.---That he investigate the case of the Milanese, as to why they refused provision to legates. (7 Kalends of March.) 525

DLXX.---To the master and brethren of the hospital called Teutonic.---He confirms the new ordinance made by them. (12 Kalends of March.) 525

DLXXI.---To the bishop of Padua.---That a perverse custom of judging be abolished. (12 Kalends of March.) 526

DLXXII.---To the bishop of Padua.---He is granted authority to absolve arsonists. (12 Kalends of March.) 526

DLXXIII.---To Henry, deacon.---He confers upon him the church under dispute and imposes silence upon his opponent. (13 Kalends of March.) 526

DLXXIV.---To C., formerly bishop of Hildesheim.---That no one, on his own authority and without the pope’s consent, move from one church to another. 527

DLXXV.---To the nobleman W., count of Caserta.---That he carefully guard enemies of the king and kingdom of Sicily who have been captured, and conduct himself with moderation. 528

DLXXVI.---To Pe[ter], bishop of Coimbra.---That everyone pay episcopal dues to his bishop. (13 Kalends of March.) 529

DLXXVII.---Oath of fealty rendered to Innocent III by Peter, prefect of the city. 529

DLXXVIII.---Oath of Count Ildebrandinus. 529

DLXXIX.---To Oddo, bishop, and the chapter of Penne.---He confirms the settlement made between the bishop of Penne and the monastery of St. Vitus of Furca. (13 Kalends of May.) 530

DLXXX.---To the king of England.---He writes on behalf of the monks of Canterbury. (Nones of March.) 531

DLXXXI.---From the suffragans of the church of Canterbury to Pope Innocent.---They reply in the case of the chapel of Lamhee. 531

DLXXXII.---From the Cistercian abbots of the kingdom of England to the pope.---On the same subject. 534

DLXXXIII.---From the monks of the church of Canterbury to the pope.---They set forth their afflictions. 536

## BOOK TWO

Year 2 of the pontificate; A.D. 1199.

I.---To the clergy, consuls, and people of Viterbo.---Concerning the persecution and punishment of heretics. (8 Kalends of April.) 537

II.---To the bishop of Melfi.---That betrothals contracted between minors, if they consent after reaching puberty, be consummated. (2 Ides of March.) 539

III.---To Guy, abbot of the monastery of St. Mary of Lundors, and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.---Concerning confirmation of privileges. (13 Kalends of April.) 540

IV.---To the consuls and people of Jesi.---That they labor diligently to restore the March to obedience to the pontiff. (16 Kalends of April.) 541

V.---To R., bishop of St. Andrews.---Unless the patrons of churches present candidates within the legal time, the right devolves upon a superior. (6 Kalends of March.) 542

VI.---To R., bishop of St. Andrews.---As the number of parishioners increases, it is lawful to build a new church. [Col. 1215] (4 Nones of March.) 542

VII.---To Matthew, bishop of Ceneda.---That fiefs and property of the Church not be alienated without the legal formalities. (10 Kalends of April.) 543

VIII.---To the patriarch of Aquileia and the bishop of Ferrara.---That by apostolic authority they undertake the care and restoration of the church of Ceneda. (8 Kalends of April.) 543

IX.---To the illustrious Miramolin, king of Morocco, and his subjects.---Notice is given of an ordinance concerning the ransom of pagan captives by Christians and of Christian captives by pagans. (8 Ides of March.) 544

X.---To the chapter of Saintes.---The statute fixing the number of canons at forty is confirmed. (6 Kalends of April.) 545

XI.---To the bishop of Poitiers.---That monks may not transfer to another order without the abbot’s permission. (13 Kalends of April.) 545

XII.---To Martin, prior, and the brethren of Camaldoli.---Possession for forty years is valid. (6 Ides of March.) 546

XIII.---To the bishop of Modena.---Rash appeals are not to be admitted. (7 Ides of March.) 546

XIV.---To the bishop of Strasbourg.---That arsonists and excommunicates not be buried in a church. (16 Kalends of April.) 546

XV.---To the prior and clerics of St. Peter outside the gate of Spoleto.---That he has confirmed the judgment rendered by a cardinal between them and the bishop of Spoleto. (16 Kalends of April.) 547

XVI.---To R., abbot of St. Julian, and I., prior of St. Gregory of Spoleto.---That they be put in possession of the adjudged property. (12 Kalends of April.) 547

XVII.---To Donatus, bishop of Alatri, and his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.---Concerning confirmation of privileges. (3 Kalends of April.) 548

XVIII.---To the dean and chapter of Avranches.---That, because of the defect previously committed in the election, they now rightly elect another bishop. (16 Kalends of April.) 549

XIX.---To the abbot of St. Mary of Casanova and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.---Concerning confirmation of privileges. (16 Kalends of April.) 550

XX.---To Lugdolf, archbishop of Magdeburg.---He grants him authority to confer ecclesiastical benefices and compel prelates to obedience. (7 Ides of April.) 551

XXI.---To the dean of the greater church of Magdeburg.---He permits him to retain the deanery of Magdeburg. (6 Kalends of April.) 551

XXII.---To the abbot and convent of St. Rufus.---That the judgment rendered in their favor by the archbishop of Lyon remain firm and ratified. (Ides of March.) 552

XXIII.---To P., cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Via Lata, legate of the Apostolic See.---He praises his diligence in reconciling the kings of France and England. (Kalends of April.) 552

XXIV.---To Philip, illustrious king of the Franks.---He approves the truce entered into between him and the king of England and exhorts him to observe it firmly. (7 Kalends of April.) 553

XXV.---To P., cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Via Lata, legate of the Apostolic See.---He declares that the truces negotiated by him between the kings of France and England please him. (3 Kalends of April.) 554

XXVI.---To the bishop of Mantua.---That he declare the chapter of Treviso freed from the claim concerning the provostship. (3 Nones of April.) 554

XXVII.---To the podestà and people of Treviso.---He exhorts them to return to the Church and amend their misdeeds. (7 Kalends of April.) 555

XXVIII.---To the illustrious king of Aragon.---He gives commands concerning genuine coinage and weight. (Nones of April.) 558

XXIX.---To the bishop of St. Andrews.---Concerning the punishment of counterfeiters. (5 Ides of March.) 559

XXX.---To the abbots of Cella St. Peter and Muri, and the provost of Uverdon.---The examination of the election of the abbot of Schaffhausen is committed to them. (7 Ides of April.) 560

XXXI.---To W., abbot of Derefordia, and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.---Concerning confirmation of privileges. (6 Ides of April.) 564

XXXII.---To the bishop of Cork and his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.---Concerning confirmation of privileges. (2 Ides of April.) 565

XXXIII.---From the bishop and podestà of Castello to the pope.---They send tribute and request the pontiff’s assistance against the people of Arezzo. 566

XXXIV.---To the archbishop of Embrun.---That he publicly declare the bishop of Vence excommunicated. (6 Ides of April.) 566

XXXV.---To the bishops of Avignon and Saint-Paul-Trois-Châteaux.---That they permit the Templars to build an oratory for themselves. [Col. 1216] (6 Ides of April.) 567

XXXVI.---To the archbishop of Bordeaux, the bishop of Agen, and the abbot of La Sauve-Majeure.---That as many canons be established in the church of Bazas as the Church’s resources permit. (2 Ides of April.) 568

[Col. 1218]
