CCXXXII. — To the Bishops of Lisbon and Coimbra. — No degree of fear or force readily rescinds a vow. (1 December.) 790

CCXXXIII. — To the Bishop of Man, the Archdeacon of Bangor, and the prior of the island of Glannav. — That betrothals are not to be contracted before the seventh year. (24 November.) 791

CCXXXIV. — To the abbot and convent of Saint Mary of Prato of Leicester. — That they are to support a certain poor man, formerly a Jew and now a Christian. (5 December.) 792

CCXXXV. — To the Abbots of Cîteaux, Morimond, and La Crête. — That, together with the Bishop of Metz, they are to examine persons suspected of heresy. (9 December.) 793

CCXXXVI. — To the Archbishop of Naples and C., priest-cardinal of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, legate of the Apostolic See. — That they are to investigate the Archbishop of Benevento. 795

CCXXXVII. — To the Chapter of Kelso. — That the goods of their church are not to be transferred to purposes other than those for which they were bestowed. (29 November.) 796

CCXXXVIII. — To the bishops and other prelates of churches established throughout the kingdom of Scotland. — That they are to refrain from injury to the monastery of Kelso. (1 December.) 797

CCXXXIX. — To Stephen, abbot, and the convent of Saint Sylvester. — That laypersons have no jurisdiction over ecclesiastical things, goods, or persons. (27 November.) 797

CCXL. — To our subdeacon Oldebert, provost of Saint Gaudentius of Novara. — That he is to have jurisdiction over his brethren. (13 December.) 802

CCXLI. — To the Bishop of Vercelli. — Excommunicated persons can neither elect nor be elected. (11 December.) 802

CCXLII. — To the Bishop of Vercelli. — That tithes are to be paid by all. 802

CCXLIII. — To the Archbishop of Canterbury, the Bishop of London, and Master W. de Sumercote, canon of Lincoln. — Concerning the penalty for one who laid violent hands upon an Apostolic judge. 804

CCXLIV. — To Adrian, Bishop of Transylvania. — An appeal indeed does not lie from a judgment and matter adjudicated; but a suspect judge may always be challenged. (14 December.) 805

CCXLV. — To the clergy, knights, and people of Capua. — Concerning the affairs of the kingdom of Sicily. 805

CCXLVI. — To the canons of Brindisi and all the clergy of the diocese of Brindisi. — That they are to obey their elect, who had cleared himself before the pope of the crimes alleged against him. (17 December.) 807

CCXLVII. — To the chapter and clergy of Ortona. 808

CCXLVIII. — To Master Henry, Archdeacon of Chiusi. (15 December.) 808

CCXLIX. — To Hilary, Archdeacon of Quiz. 809

CCL. — To Master Henry, canon of the church of Saint Michael in Transylvania. (15 December.) 809

CCLI. — To the illustrious King of the Franks. — That he is to send aid to the King of Jerusalem against the Saracens, and write to the Emperor of the Greeks that he should refrain from internal wars against Christians. 809

CCLII. — Letter of Leo, King of the Armenians, to Pope Innocent. — He implores Apostolic assistance. 810

CCLIII. — To Leo, illustrious King of Armenia. — He replies to the preceding letter. (25 December.) 813

CCLIV. — To the noble Counts Paganus and Arron, and to all other barons, knights, and people established in the kingdom of our dearest son in Christ, Leo, illustrious King of Armenia. — That they are to conduct themselves courageously with their king against the Saracens. (17 December.) 814

CCLV. — To the illustrious King of Armenia. — He sends the banner of Saint Peter, for use against the enemies of the Cross. (17 December.) 815

[Col. 1223]

CCLVI. — To all the people of the city of Castellana. — He grants them a rector in accordance with the citizens’ request. (22 December.) 815

CCLVII. — To the Patriarch of Jerusalem, the Archbishop of Tyre, and the Bishop of Acre. — That they are to rescind an unjustly issued sentence of excommunication and punish the bishop who rashly pronounced it. (15 December.) 816

CCLVIII. — To the clergy and people of Città. — That they are to receive the Count of Theate as their guardian. (30 December.) 818

CCLIX. — To the illustrious King of Armenia. — That he is to restore the castle of Gaston to the Templars. 819

CCLX. — To the Prior of Saint Victor, and Masters L., canon of Bologna, and Ubertus, canon of Modena. — Concerning the accusations and canonical purgation of the Abbot of Pomposa. (2 December.) 820

CCLXI. — To the Archbishop of Rossano. — He answers him on certain questions. (31 December.) 822

CCLXII. — To A., viscount of Fermo. — He entrusts several prefectures to him. 823

CCLXIII, CCLXIV. — To Master Guido, archpriest of the parish church of the city. (31 December.) 824

CCLXV. — To the Abbot of Saint Ulrich, the schoolmaster, and [lacuna] the custodian of Augsburg. — That fraud is not to benefit a person who falsely claims to have obtained something from the Apostolic See. 824

CCLXVI. — To the nobleman Johnnitius. — That he is to receive the Apostolic legate reverently. 825

CCLXVII. — To the provost and brethren of Saint Stephen in Broglio. — That they are to receive Al. Marcellinus as a canon. (10 January.) 825

CCLXVIII. — To the Abbots of Cîteaux, Clairvaux, Pontigny, La Ferté, and to all abbots of the Cistercian Order. — That they are to devote a fiftieth part of their property to the needs of the holy war. (28 December.) 826

CCLXIX. — To the Abbot of Prémontré. — On the same matter. 828

CCLXX. — To the Archbishop of Magdeburg and his suffragans, abbots, and all clerics established in the province of Magdeburg. — That they are to assist Christians in the East with money and men against the Saracens. (31 December.) 828

CCLXXI. — To all Christ’s faithful established throughout the province of Vienne. — On the same matter. (4 January.) 832

CCLXXII. — To abbots, priors, and all prelates of exempt churches established in the province of Milan. — That they are to devote a fortieth part of all their property to the holy war. (30 December.) 835

CCLXXIII. — To the Archbishop of Tyre and the Bishop of Sidon. — The case pending between the church of Tripoli and the Hospitallers is entrusted to them. 836

CCLXXIV. — To the Abbot of Saint Mary of Ferraria and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life in perpetuity. — Concerning confirmation of their privileges. (19 January.) 837

CCLXXV. — To the Bishop of Padua. — That he is to assign to Master G. the first prebend that falls vacant. 838

CCLXXVI. — To Master John, our subdeacon and notary. — He confirms a judgment delivered in his favour. 839

CCLXXVII. — To the Archdeacon and Chapter of Capua. — He discusses various matters concerning the election and postulation of prelates. 841

CCLXXVIII. — To the Bishop of Bamberg and Master Prévostin, schoolmaster of Mainz. — That bishops cannot be transferred from one church to another without the authority of the Roman Pontiff. (26 January.) 845

CCLXXIX. — To Theobald, Bishop of Amiens. — He confirms a certain statute and ordinance of his. (28 January.) 847

CCLXXX. — To the counts, barons, bailiffs, judges, citizens, and all the people established in the kingdom of Sicily. — That they are to contribute resources and counsel with the Apostolic legate for the preservation of the kingdom. (3 February.) 848

CCLXXXI. — To the master and brethren of the Knights Templar established in Slavonia. — He confirms a certain settlement. (25 January.) 849

CCLXXXII. — To the Bishop, dean, and subdean of Lincoln. — That a resignation extorted by force or fear is not binding. (5 February.) 850

CCLXXXIII. — To the archpriest and canons of Sutri. — Concerning the right of election with respect to possessory and petitory proceedings. 851

CCLXXXIV. — To the Archbishop of Tours. — That an archbishop may, because of illness, delegate the consecration of suffragans. 852

CCLXXXV. — To the Bishop of the city of Castellana. — That the citizens are to be released from sentences of excommunication and interdict. 852

[Col. 1224]

CCLXXXVI. — To Raynerius, abbot, and the convent of Saint Peter of Gubbio. — He confirms their ancient privileges. 852

CCLXXXVII. — To the Abbot of La Ferté and G. and F., Archdeacons of Chalon. — He entrusts to them the case of the Church of Autun and the monastery of Baume. 852

CCLXXXVIII. — To the Bishop and dean of Paderborn and the Abbot of Helmarshausen. — That they are to assist the Bishop-elect of Hildesheim. (2 February.) 852

CCLXXXIX. — To the Abbots of Sichen and the Valley of Blessed George, and to the provost of Saint Mary at Herford. — Concerning the devolution of prebends if they are not conferred within the time fixed by law. (16 February.) 854

CCXC. — To all prelates and clerics of the diocese of Penne. — That they are to render account to their bishop concerning mortuary tithes and offerings. (15 March.) 857

CCXCI. — To Hildebrand, Bishop of Volterra. — Concerning confirmation of privileges. (24 March.) 857

CCXCII. — To Willelmod Bieria, priest. — He is received under Apostolic protection. (28 April.) 858

CCXCIII, CCXCIV. — See the note. 858

CCXCV. — To the Bishop of Vercelli and the Abbot of Lucedio. — A certain case of Milan is entrusted to them. (24 May.) 859

CCXCVI. — To John, Prior of Mariadura, and his brethren, present and future. — Concerning confirmation of privileges. (4 July.) 859

CCXCVII. — To William, lord of Montpellier. — He is received under the protection of the Apostolic See. (10 July.) 861

CCXCVIII. — To the same. — He announces that he is sending a legate against heretics. (10 July.) 861

CCXCIX. — To the Bishops of Tinin and Skradin and the Abbot of Trogir. — Concerning the election of the Bishop of Hvar. (12 July.) 862

CCC. — To the Chapter of Split. — On the same matter. (14 July.) 863

CCCI. — To the Bishop, dean, and chapter of Paris. — The settlement made between the Archdeacon of Paris and the Abbess of Cala is confirmed. (1 December.) 864

CCCII. — Constitution concerning the Jews. (15 September.) 864

CCCIII. — To the abbot and convent of Virziliac. — He grants an indulgence of forty days. (5 November.) 865

CCCIV. — To Grumerius, Bishop of Piacenza. — Concerning confirmation of privileges. (6 November.) 865

CCCV. — To the abbots, priors, and all prelates of exempt churches established in the province of Rouen. — Concerning aid for the Holy Land. (5 January.) 868

**BOOK THREE. — Third year of the pontificate, A.D. 1200.**

I. — To N. [lacuna], perhaps Bishop of Ely; to the Abbot of Saint Edmund’s; and to the Prior of Canterbury. — Concerning the affair of the Bishop of Glastonbury with the monks of Glastonbury. 869

II. — To the Archbishop of Split. — He commands him publicly to declare excommunicated Nicholas, Bishop of Hvar, who had procured the election, as bishops in the province of Split, of two men not yet constituted in sacred orders. (14 October.) 870

III. — To Hemmerad, King of the Hungarians. — He declares what penalties he has established for heretics, and commands him to pursue them and Ban Kulin, supporter of heretics, and to proscribe them from the kingdom of Hungary after confiscating their goods. (11 October.) 871

IV. — [Lacuna.] — He decrees that the abbot and monks of the monastery of Lorsch are suspended, because of excommunication, until the pope’s pleasure. (Before 27 August.) 873

V. — To the illustrious King of Connacht. — He writes what is to be decided concerning those fleeing to churches. 875

VI. — To the consuls and people of Novara. — He rebukes the people of Novara because they compelled their bishop to go into exile; he warns them to repent, otherwise he will pronounce canonical sentences against them. (17 October.) 876

VII. — To the chapter, abbots, and all the clergy of Novara. — On the same matter. (17 October.) 878

VIII. — To the Abbot of Hautvillers. — He commands him fraternally to receive into the monastery J. [lacuna], a deacon who, having omitted the acolyte’s order, had been promoted to sacred orders. He orders that, after receiving the order of acolyte, he may be ordained priest. (19 October.) 878

IX. — To the Archbishop of Pisa. — Whether his consent, as Primate of Sardinia, must be sought in the elections of metropolitan bishops subject to him. (17 October.) 879

X. — To the Bishop of Penne. (29 October.) 880

XI. — To the Queen of the Franks. — Concerning the divorce affair with the King of the Franks. (31 October.) 881

XII. — To the King of the Danes. — On the same matter. 883

XIII. — Letter of Odo, Bishop of Paris, to the Pope. — He reports what has been done between the king and queen in the matter of divorce. 884

XIV. — Letter of the Bishop of Soissons. — On the same matter. 885

XV. — Letter of Octavian, Bishop of Ostia. — He reports what he has done in the matter of the marriage between the King and Queen of the Franks. 887

XVI. — To O., Bishop of Ostia, legate of the Apostolic See. — He replies to the preceding letter and prescribes what is to be done in that affair. 891

XVII. — Letter of Philip II, King of the Franks. — He reports that he has reverently received the Apostolic legate, and discusses the divorce case. (Written after 8 December.) 895

XVIII. — To the illustrious King of the Franks. — He replies to the preceding letter and warns him to obey the commands of the Apostolic legate. 896

XIX. — To the Bishop of Lincoln. — Concerning one who accidentally crushed a boy with a horse and thereafter did not celebrate the divine mysteries. (8 November.) 898

XX. — To O., Bishop of Ostia, legate of the Apostolic See. — He absolves the Bishop of Auxerre from a sentence of suspension, though rejecting his election to the archbishopric of Sens. (8 November.) 898

XXI. — To the consuls and people of Zadar. — He warns and commands them not to obstruct appeals brought before the Apostolic See. 900

XXII. — To the nobleman S. [lacuna], Count of Ragusa. — He praises him for his reverence toward the Apostolic See and loyalty to the King of Sicily. 901

XXIII. — To the archbishops, counts, barons, citizens, and all the people established throughout Apulia. — He urges them to resist Markward. 901

XXIV. — To J., priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Prisca, legate of the Apostolic See. — He commands him to punish heretics in the province of Narbonne in accordance with canonical sanctions. 903

XXV. — To Peter, Bishop of Arras. — He grants permission for him to confer benefices upon suitable persons, and upon others by Apostolic mandate. (28 November.) 906

XXVI. — To the Archpriest of Padua, Peregrine, Archdeacon of Trent, and the Dean of Saint Felix of Aquileia. — On behalf of the Bishop of Ceneda, to whom he assigns the provostship of Saint Stephen of Aquileia; he entrusts to them the question whether he ought by right to be admitted to it. (25 November.) 907

XXVII. — To Pantaleon, Archbishop of Conza. — He entrusts to him the task of settling, together with his suffragans, the disputes between Latins and Greeks of his diocese, when one party refuses to take part in the divine offices of the other. (23 November.) 909

XXVIII. — To the podestà and people of Fermo. — Concerning the return of the March and of the people of Fermo to obedience to the Apostolic See; and concerning measures to be established for the good of peace by the legate and representatives of that See. 910

XXIX. — To the consuls and people of Fano. — On the same matter, and concerning payment of the annual tribute. 912

XXX. — To the podestà and men of Sant’Elpidio. — Concerning a certain appeal made by them to the Apostolic See. 914

XXXI. — To the podestà and men of Monte Rubiano. — That they are to obey the commands of the envoys of the Apostolic See concerning peace with the people of Fermo. 914

XXXII. — To the Bishop of Modena and Master Hubert, canon of Modena. — He entrusts to them an inquiry into why the Bishop of Bologna ordained Albert, Bishop-elect of Imola, simultaneously deacon and priest. 915

XXXIII. — To John Rustici, citizen of Fano. — He grants him a vineyard. 916

XXXIV. — To the Bishop of Metz. — Concerning one who accidentally crushed a boy. (24 November.) 916

XXXV. — To the nobleman, the Judge of Cagliari. — He rebukes him for many disgraceful acts and commands him to come to the Apostolic See, personally or through representatives, in order to clear himself of them. 917

XXXVI. — To the Archbishop of Cagliari. — That he is to investigate the matters set out above. 918

XXXVII. — To the Archbishop of Bar. — Concerning false Apostolic letters brought to him, and concerning Dominic, formerly Bishop of Suacium, who is to be placed in close custody. (5 December.) 919

XXXVIII. — To L. of Vicobaldon and I. of Vigalon, provosts; [lacuna] of Rundenario and Saint Christopher of Laude; to the chapters and all brethren of the same profession. — He urges them, since they live according to a religious purpose, to draw up rules and send them to the Apostolic See. 921

XXXIX. — To the podestà and people of Treviso. — He grants that, since they are prepared to make satisfaction to the Church for the killing of the Bishop of Belluno, they may be released by the Bishop of Ferrara from the sentence of interdict, due safeguards having been observed. (13 November.) 922

XL. — To N. [lacuna] of Albaripa and [lacuna] of Moris, abbots, and [lacuna] prior of Clairvaux. — That no one may rashly dare to violate the agreements between the widow of the Count of Flanders and Count Baldwin. (8 December.) 926

XLI. — To [lacuna] Bishop, [lacuna] Abbot of Saint Victor, and Master P., provincial, canon of Saint Marcellus, of Paris. — He entrusts to them the decision of the case concerning the provostship of Ciklin. (8 December.) 927

XLII. — To the Archbishop of Armagh and the Bishops of Clonfert and Down. — Concerning the election of the Bishop of Ardfert in Ireland. 929

XLIII. — [Lacuna.] — He grants that the elect of Bourges may clear himself of contempt of the interdict; and that, after his oath and absolution, the pallium may be given him. (26 January.) 930

XLIV. — To the Archbishop of Naples. — In consideration of his merits, he grants him the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. 931

XLV. — To the master and brethren of the Knights Templar of Paris. — He confirms a certain judgment given for them concerning a prebend. (31 January.) 932

XLVI. — To Odo, our subdeacon and chaplain, and Albertinus, notary of our chamber, our agents. — He entrusts to them the question of which castles are to be restored to the people of Fermo by the inhabitants of Monte Rubiano. (1 February.) 933

XLVII. — To N. [lacuna], Abbots of Cuissy and Mont-Saint-Martin. — He urges them to furnish assistance for the liberation of the Holy Land. (5 February.) 934

XLVIII. — To the podestà and people of Ancona. — Concerning their return to obedience to the Apostolic See. 936

XLIX. — To all persons, clerics as well as laypersons, established in the March. — On the same matter. 937

L. — To O., our subdeacon and chaplain, and A., notary of our chamber, our agents. — Concerning their authority in administering the affairs of the Apostolic See in the March. 937

LI. — To the consuls and people of Senigallia. — He commands them to restore the castles and other things which they have occupied in the bishopric of Senigallia. 938

LII. — To the consuls and people of Fano. — He commands them to restore what has been taken from the Roman Church; concerning the annual tribute to be paid to the Roman Church for the city and county of Fano. 939

LIII. — To the consuls and people of Camerino. — Concerning the annual tribute to be paid to the Roman Church for the city of Camerino. He rebukes them because they destroyed the valley of the castle of Makelde and occupied the castle of Saint Anatolia. 940

LIV. — To the Abbot of Stenwelt, the provost of Saint Severin at Cologne, and [lacuna] prior of Mere. — Concerning the election of the abbess of Gerresheim. (6 February.) 940

LV. — To the prior and chapter of Segunti. — Concerning confirmation of certain revenues. (13 February.) 943

LVI. — To the prior and regular canons of the church of Saint Mary of Chirberi. — Concerning confirmation of privileges. (1 February.) 944

LVII. — To the nobleman Aymo, lord of Cicala, royal justiciar of the Terra di Lavoro. — He is received under protection. (16 February.) 945

*(Book Four is missing and is still sought.)*

**BOOK FIVE. — Fifth year of the pontificate, A.D. 1202.**

I. — To the Bishop of
To the bishop of Pistoia.—Concerning the absolution by their own bishop of excommunicated nuns. (III Kalends of March.) 945

II.—To Adhemar, prior of Grandmont, and his brethren, present and future, regularly established.—He confirms their privileges. (III Kalends of March.) 945

III.—To the prior and brethren of Grandmont.—He revokes the agreement within the Order of Grandmont. (III Kalends of March.) 946

IV.—To the podestà, councillors, and people of Pisa.—That the Pisans are not to support Markward. (IV Nones of March.) 950

V.—To Ignatius, prior, and the clerics of St Gregory of Spoleto.—The disputes between the bishop of Spoleto and the prior and clerics of St Gregory are settled. (VI Nones of March.) 952

VI.—To the archbishop of Ravenna.—Concerning the transfer of the bishop of Imola to the church of Ravenna. (VI Ides of March.) 955

VII.—To Master Simon of Melun, canon of Hereford.—The sons of two co-godfathers may not be joined in marriage. (XV Kalends of April.) 957

VIII.—To the bishop of Palestrina, legate of the Apostolic See.—He orders him, as a precaution, to absolve the archbishop of Magdeburg. (XII Kalends of April.) 957

IX.—To Walter, provost of St Peter of Mont-Serein, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life. [Col. 1227]—Concerning confirmation of their privileges. (XII Kalends of April.) 959

X.—To the provost and convent of Mont-Serein.—They are granted permission to eat meat. (XI Kalends of April.) 960

XI.—To the archbishop of Sens.—For the absolution of the bishop of Nevers. (XVII Kalends of April.) 961

XII.—To the abbot of St Denis; the prior of St Martin-des-Champs; and J., master of the schools of Orléans.—Concerning the receiving of the canonical purgation of the archdeacon of Chartres. (IX Kalends of April.) 961

XIII.—To the bishop of Palestrina, legate of the Apostolic See, and to the abbots of St Benedict and of Belle-Lieu, of the Cistercian Order, in the diocese of Verdun.—Concerning the accusation against the bishop of Toul. (V Kalends of April.) 963

XIV.—To the canons of Mainz.—The election of the archbishop of Mainz is confirmed. (X Kalends of April.) 964

XV.—To Siffrid, archbishop of Mainz.—Concerning the same matter. (XII Kalends of April.) 969

XVI.—To the bishop of Chalon and the abbot of Cîteaux.—Concerning the release of the abbot of Saint-Seine from his vow to cross the sea to the Holy Land. (V Ides of April.) 970

XVII.—To the chapter of Ragusa.—Permission is granted to elect another archbishop because of the archbishop’s prolonged absence. 970

XVIII.—To the illustrious king of Hungary.—The king is exhorted to devotion to the Apostolic See. 971

XIX.—To the bishop-elect of Cambrai.—Concerning the making good of prelates’ negligence. (XVI Kalends of April.) 971

XX.—To the illustrious king of England.—The king is invited to works of piety. (VI Kalends of April.) 972

XXI.—To Brother G. of the Order of the Temple, our familiar and a nobleman; and to L. and M. of Potenza, masters chamberlains of Apulia, the Terra di Lavoro, and the duchy of Amalfi.—The acts performed by W. of Plear are annulled. (V Kalends of May.) 973

XXII.—To the archbishops, bishops, abbots, priors, and all clergy; counts, barons, citizens, and others established throughout Apulia, the Terra di Lavoro, and the duchy of Amalfi.—Provision is made for the government of Apulia and the Terra di Lavoro. (X Kalends of April.) 974

XXIII.—To the bishop of Worcester.—Concerning the right to appeal to the Apostolic See. (X Kalends of May.) 974

XXIV.—To the same.—Appeals are not always to be heeded. (VIII Kalends of May.) 975

XXV.—To the dean and chapter of Châlons.—Concerning the election of the bishop of Châlons. 976

XXVI.—To the patriarchs, archbishops, bishops, abbots, priors, and all clergy established in the lands overseas.—Concerning legates sent to the Holy Land. 977

XXVII.—To the priest-cardinal of St Praxedes, legate of the Apostolic See.—The legation to the East is entrusted to him. 979

XXVIII.—To the chapter of Angers.—Concerning the election of the bishop of Angers. (IV Kalends of May.) 980

XXIX.—To the chapter of Prague.—Concerning the absolution of the bishop of Prague. (III Nones of May.) 981

XXX.—To the nobleman …, count of Tropea. 984

XXXI.—To the archbishop of Rouen.—That he punish the rebels against the king of England. (Nones of March.) 984

XXXII.—To A. …, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, bishop of Verona.—Concerning the archdeaconry of Verona. (VI Ides of May.) 985

XXXIII.—To the same.—Against improper appeals. 986

XXXIV.—To the same.—On the same subject. 987

XXXV.—To the same.—Concerning the dispute of the archdeacon of Verona. 987

XXXVI.—To the archbishop of Bourges, the bishop of Nevers, and the abbot of Cluny.—How proceedings are to be conducted against those suspected of heresy. (IV Ides of May.) 989

XXXVII.—To Jovinus, master of the schools of Orléans.—Concerning the election of the prior of Gracay. (Ides of May.) 990

XXXVIII.—To the archbishops, bishops, and other prelates of churches; counts, barons, citizens, and others established throughout the kingdom of Sicily.—Concerning the case of Walter of Brienne. 993

XXXIX.—To Bishop P., elected archbishop of Palermo, a royal familiar, etc.—That he assist Walter of Brienne. 996

XL.—To the bishop of Auxerre.—What is understood by the term “clerics,” and which persons are reckoned to die intestate. 998

XLI.—To the bishop of Noyon.—How proceedings ought to be conducted when the issue is ownership. (V Kalends of June.) 998

XLII.—To the chapter of Siponto.—Concerning the rank and authority of the archbishop of Siponto. (VIII Kalends of June.) 999

XLIII.—Letter of the king of the Armenians to the lord pope.—He replies [Col. 1228] to the letters which the pope had written to him. (1 October, 1201.) 1003

XLIV.—To L., illustrious king of the Armenians.—That the king and kingdom of Armenia may not be excommunicated or placed under interdict except by the pope’s special mandate. (Kalends of June.) 1007

XLV.—Letter of the Catholicos of the Armenians to the lord pope.—Concerning the primacy of the pope and the persecutions of the Armenian Church. 1007

XLVI.—To the Catholicos of the Armenians.—He replies to the preceding letter. (Kalends of July.) 1010

XLVII.—Letter of the archbishop of Sis, chancellor of the king of Armenia, to the lord pope.—He requests a mitre, pallium, and indulgence. 1012

XLVIII.—Reply to the archbishop of Sis.—He replies to the preceding letter and sends him a pallium. (Kalends of June.) 1013

XLIX.—To the archbishop of Reims, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, legate of the Apostolic See.—Concerning the divorce of Philip, king of the French. (III Nones of July.) 1014

L.—To the illustrious king of the French.—On the same subject. (III Ides of July.) 1015

LI.—To the nobleman James, our cousin and marshal.—Concerning the marriage of the king of Sicily to the sister of the king of Aragon. (Nones of June.) 1018

LII.—To the archbishop of Bourges.—A marriage which has endured for a long time is not lightly to be challenged. (II Nones of June.) 1019

LIII.—To the nobleman Andrew of Calvignac.—Concerning the same matter. (II Nones of June.) 1020

LIV.—To Master Honorius, archdeacon of Richmond.—The dispute concerning the archdeaconry of Richmond is determined. (II Nones of June.) 1021

LV.—To the dean and chapter of York.—Concerning the same matter. (III Nones of June.) 1025

LVI.—To the king of England.—On the same subject. (III Nones of June.) 1026

LVII.—To the archbishop of Canterbury.—Concerning the judgment of the abbot of Thorney. (II Nones of June.) 1026

LVIII.—To the same.—He is granted authority to institute archdeacons. (II Kalends of June.) 1029

LIX.—To the bishop of Ely, the dean of Lincoln, and the archdeacon of Bedford.—They are commissioned to investigate the accusation brought against the archbishop of York. (II Kalends of June.) 1029

LX.—To the archbishop of Messina.—He relaxes the sentence of excommunication by which the archbishop of Messina was bound. (XIII Kalends of June.) 1030

LXI.—To the abbot and convent of Cîteaux.—Against deserters from the Cistercian Order. (XIV Kalends of July.) 1031

LXII.—To John, former archbishop of Lyons.—He sends the collects concerning St Bernard. (VI Ides of June.) 1032

LXIII.—To the chapter of Capua.—The church of Capua is commended to the archbishop of Salerno. (II Ides of June.) 1033

LXIV.—To P., priest-cardinal of the title of St Marcellus, legate of the Apostolic See.—He is granted authority to make a will. (III Ides of June.) 1033

LXV.—To the bishop of Exeter. (XIII Kalends of May.) 1034

LXVI.—To the same.—That sons may not succeed their fathers in ecclesiastical benefices. (IV Ides of June.) 1034

LXVII.—To the abbess and nuns of Remiremont.—Concerning the same matter. (III Ides of June.) 1035

LXVIII.—To John, illustrious king of England.—He is reproved for what he had done against the bishop of Limoges. 1036

LXIX.—To the bishop of Besançon; and to the Marsican, our subdeacon and chaplain.—Concerning the election of the archbishop of Trani. (VIII Kalends of July.) 1037

LXX.—To the prior and chapter of Sées.—Concerning the election of the bishop of Sées. (VIII Kalends of July.) 1038

LXXI.—To H., dean of the greater church of Cologne, provost of Bonn, and prior of Heisterbach.—Concerning the election of the abbess of Gerresheim. (VI Kalends of July.) 1044

LXXII.—To the abbot and convent of Dol.—The agreement entered into with the lord of the castle of Ralph is confirmed. (III Kalends of July.) 1048

LXXIII.—To Claromont, canon of Thérouanne.—His prebend is confirmed. (VII Ides of July.) 1050

LXXIV.—To the archbishop of Arles and the abbots of St Giles and Valmagne.—Concerning the accusation against the abbot of St William and his deposition. (VIII Ides of August.) 1053

LXXV.—To the bishop, archdeacon, and provost of Piacenza.—Concerning the contumacy of the clerics of St Antoninus of Piacenza. (V Ides of August.) 1057

LXXVI.—To the archbishop of Amalfi.—Concerning the affairs of the kingdom of Sicily. 1060

LXXVII.—To Rain, canon of Ferentino.—Churches [Col. 1229] may not be given to monasteries without the permission of their own bishop. 1061

LXXVIII.—To the prior and brethren living the regular life near the cave of Blessed Benedict.—He grants them six pounds of the customary currency annually. (Kalends of September.) 1062

LXXIX.—To the bishop of Orkney.—Concerning the bishop of Catania, whose tongue had been cut out. 1062

LXXX.—To the archbishops, bishops, abbots, priors to whom these letters shall come.—Concerning the penance imposed upon one who first killed his daughter and then his wife because of hunger. (III Nones of September.) 1063

LXXXI.—To the abbot and chapter of St John of Sens.—Permission is granted that no one may pronounce a sentence of interdict or excommunication against that monastery. (Nones of September.) 1064

LXXXII.—To the abbot and convent of Subiaco.—Concerning certain faults which had crept in among the monks and were to be corrected. 1064

LXXXIII.—To the priest-cardinal of the title of St Stephen on the Caelian Hill, legate of the Apostolic See.—Concerning the election of the archbishop of Armagh. 1066

LXXXIV.—To Walter, count of Brienne, master justiciar of the Terra di Lavoro.—That he depart without delay for Sicily against Markward. (XVIII Kalends of October.) 1070

LXXXV.—To the nobleman James, our cousin and marshal, master justiciar and captain of all Apulia and the Terra di Lavoro.—That he join Walter, count of Brienne, as he proceeds to Sicily, and that provision be made for his expenses. (XVIII Kalends of October.) 1072

LXXXVI.—To all merchants to whom these letters come.—He pledges himself on behalf of Walter, count of Brienne, up to 3,000 ounces. 1072

LXXXVII.—To Brother Richard and Eugene, masters chamberlains of Apulia and the Terra di Lavoro.—That the revenues of their territories be pledged for Walter, count of Brienne. 1073

LXXXVIII.—To the chapter of Trani.—Concerning the election of an archbishop. (XVI Kalends of October.) 1073

LXXXIX.—To C., archbishop of Monreale, and Parisio, bishop-elect of Palermo, familiars of the king of Sicily.—Concerning the death of Markward. (VIII Kalends of October.) 1075

XC.—To the bishop of Ely, the abbot of St Edmund, and the prior of Canterbury.—Concerning the ordering of the churches of Bath and Glastonbury. (VIII Kalends of October.) 1076

XCI.—To the bishop of Ely.—Concerning a settlement pertaining to the monastery of St Edmund. (XII Kalends of October.) 1083

XCII.—To the bishop of Ely, the abbot of St Edmund, and the prior of Canterbury.—On the same subject as in letter 90. (IV Kalends of October.) 1085

XCIII.—To the bishop of Viterbo.—Confirmation of the endowment of the church of St Mary of Palenzano and of the castle of Balnaria, made to it by the consuls of Viterbo. (II Nones of October.) 1087

XCIV.—To the bishop of Ely and the abbot of St Edmund.—He gives them the task of examining whether certain noblemen ought, at the request of the king of England, to be dispensed from their crusading vow. 1088

XCV.—To the archbishop of Lyons.—He writes concerning the penalties to be imposed on clerics committing offences. (VII Ides of October.) 1090

XCVI.—To the chapter of Auch.—That proceedings for deprivation be brought against an archbishop suffering from epilepsy, in accordance with the decree of Pope Gelasius. (IV Nones of November.) 1091

XCVII.—To the bishop of Verona, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church.—Concerning the granting of a canonry at Verona. (II Kalends of November.) 1094

XCVIII.—To the chancellor and Master Lothar, canon of Paris.—Concerning the agreement between the Hospitallers of Cerisiers and the abbot and convent of the monastery of Scarlieu. (II Nones of November.) 1094

XCIX.—To Siffrid, archbishop of Mainz, the bishop of Würzburg, and the abbot of Salem.—Concerning the election of the bishop of Augsburg. (VII Ides of November.) 1095

C.—To the bishop of Paris and to John, abbot, and the chapter of St Geneviève, Paris.—He confirms by apostolic authority the settlement made between them concerning parochial right in the parish of Mont-sur-Chapelle. (VII Ides of November.) 1097

CI.—To the archbishop of Lyons.—He writes concerning penalties to be imposed on clerics who commit offences, and decrees that those deprived of office are to be confined in a monastery. (VI Ides of November.) 1098

CII.—To the archbishops and bishops established in the kingdom of Hungary.—Concerning the provostships of the kingdom of Hungary subject to the Apostolic See. (VI Ides of November.) 1099

[CIII.] [Col. 1230]—To H. …, illustrious king of Hungary.—He exhorts him to fulfil his vow to proceed to the Holy Land. 1100

CIV.—To Roger, abbot of the monastery of Blessed Peter and Paul and St Augustine, situated near the metropolitan church of Canterbury, and his brethren.—He receives them under the protection of Blessed Peter, and their possessions and privileges are enumerated. (II Nones of November.) 1101

CV.—To the bishop and chapter of Metz.—Although the bishop did not request one, he gives him a coadjutor because he had lost the sight of his eyes. (II Ides of November.) 1103

CVI.—To the chapter of Amalfi.—He confirms by apostolic authority M., archdeacon of Teano, elected archbishop of Amalfi by their envoys. (XVII Kalends of November.) 1104

CVII.—To the archbishop of Besançon, the archdeacon of Senlis, and all rectors of churches established throughout the diocese of Besançon.—That Cistercian monks are not to be drawn before secular courts. (Ides of November.) 1106

CVIII.—To R., priest-cardinal of the title of SS Marcellus and Peter, abbot of Monte Cassino.—He grants him permission to receive two castles from Robert of Aquila. (II Kalends of December.) 1106

CIX.—To the abbots of Cîteaux, La Ferté, Pontigny, Clairvaux, and Morimond.—An exhortatory letter to remain in the simplicity of the Rule. (X Kalends of December.) 1107

CX.—To B., archbishop of Split, and J., our chaplain.—Concerning the expulsion of the Cathars. (XI Kalends of December.) 1108

CXI.—To the nobleman Henry, duke of Silesia.—He confirms the agreement concluded between him and his uncle. (VII Kalends of December.) 1110

CXII.—To N. …, archbishop of Gniezno; and to the bishops of … Cracow and Wrocław.—On the same subject. (VII Kalends of December.) 1110

CXIII.—To the bishop of Wrocław.—Concerning one who was promoted first to the diaconate and immediately afterward to the priesthood. (X Kalends of December.) 1111

CXIV.—To the bishop of Paris.—That he cause to be observed in his diocese the sentence pronounced by the archbishop of Sens, because the abbot of St Magloire and the prior of Chastres had refused him the procurations due by reason of visitation. (IV Kalends of December.) 1111

CXV.—Letter of Kalojan, emperor of the Bulgarians, to the pope. 1112

CXVI.—To Kalojan, lord of the Vlachs and Bulgarians.—He replies to the preceding letter. (V Kalends of December.) 1113

CXVII.—Letter of Basil, archbishop of Zagora, to the pope.—He gives thanks to the pope. 1115

CXVIII.—Letter of Bellota, prince, to the pontiff.—He seeks communion with the Roman Church. 1116

CXIX.—To Basil, archbishop of Zagora.—He replies to letter 117. 1116

CXX.—To the nobleman Prince Bellota, his … wife and children.—He replies to letter 118. (V Kalends of December.) 1118

CXXI.—To John, formerly archbishop of Lyons.—He explains everything said in the Mass concerning the consecration and other matters. (III Kalends of December.) 1118

CXXII.—To the illustrious emperor of Constantinople.—Concerning the affairs of the empire. (XVI Kalends of December.) 1123

CXXIII.—To the provost of Vercelli and Master Widotto of Maio, canon of Novara.—Concerning certain prebends in the church of Genoa. (III Kalends of December.) 1125

CXXIV.—To the archbishop of Pisa.—That he not misuse, without the approval of the Apostolic See, the oath sworn to him by C. …, judge of Torres, since that judge is subject to the Apostolic See by feudal right. (II Nones of December.) 1126

CXXV.—To the nobleman C. …, judge of Torres.—On the same subject. (II Nones of December.) 1127

CXXVI.—To the bishop, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, and the prior of St George, of Verona.—Concerning a fief in the church of Vicenza. 1128

CXXVII.—To P. of Stuibald, our brother-in-law and seneschal.—He grants him the castle of Giuliano in trust. (Nones of December.) 1129

CXXVIII.—To the nobleman William, lord of Montpellier.—Concerning the legitimisation of children. (After VII Ides of September.) 1130

CXXIX.—To the bishops of Ely and Norwich.—He orders that the man presented by the monks of Durham be instituted. (Ides of December.) 1134

CXXX.—To Agnes, abbess of the monastery of Jouarre, and her successors, present and future, professing the monastic life, in perpetuity.—Their privileges are confirmed. (Kalends of December.) 1135

CXXXI.—To the bishop of Nevers.—That he now confer upon the nephew of the said Blasius the benefice of three marks formerly granted by his predecessor, Master Blasius, papal subdeacon and notary, now bishop-elect of Torres. [Col. 1231] 1137

CXXXII.—To the abbot of Dol and Henry, papal subdeacon, prior of Leproso.—That they cause Master P. … of Vico to be received as canon and brother by the chapter of Bourges, if the greater part of the chapter agrees, notwithstanding the opposition of the dean and certain others. 1137

CXXXIII.—To the bishop and chapter of Angoulême.—He recommends a certain cleric for reception as a canon. (XIV Kalends of January.) 1138

CXXXIV.—To the archbishop of Mainz.—That he not favour Philip, duke of Swabia, against the bishop of Würzburg, and that he ensure firm observance of the sentences pronounced by that bishop against wrongdoers. (X Kalends of January.) 1139

CXXXV.—To the bishop of Ely.—Concerning the granting of a benefice by the monks of Durham. (Nones of January.) 1140

CXXXVI.—To the archbishop of Bourges and the bishop of Clermont.—He orders them to proceed against the prior and monks of St Pourçain, who had inflicted injuries on the brethren of the Order of the Temple and, disregarding the apostolic command, refused to make satisfaction to them. (VI Ides of December.) 1141

CXXXVII.—To the bishop-elect of Châlons and the abbot of Trois-Fontaines.—He gives them the task of examining the privileges of the abbess and nuns of the monastery of Jouarre. (IV Ides of January.) 1144

CXXXVIII.—To the bishop of Chiusi; O., castellan of Radicofani; and the acolyte and Master P., our scribe.—Concerning Napoleon and Popone, committed to prison after the agreement between the Romans and the people of Viterbo, and concerning their custody in the fortress of Lariano. (IV Ides of January.) 1147

CXXXIX.—To the cantor and chapter of St Front of Périgueux.—Concerning the granting of a prebend. (Ides of January.) 1149

CXL.—To the prior of St Fridianus of Lucca and Master B. Fascalo, canon of Pisa.—Concerning the election of the bishop of Lucca. (V Ides of January.) 1150

CXLI.—To the archbishop of Sens.—He entrusts to him the determination of the case concerning the exchange of the archdeaconry and provostship between Masters S. … and B. …. (Ides of January.) 1152

CXLII.—To the abbot of Dol and Eug., papal subdeacon, prior of Leproso.—That they compel the bishop of Nevers to assign, in accordance with the pope’s command, a prebend to the nephew of P. …, bishop-elect of Torres. (Ides of January.) 1154

CXLIII.—To the abbots of Caen, Troarn, and Val-Richer.—He orders them to restrain the bishop of Lisieux from the unjust harassment of Hugh of Rochepierre concerning the archdeaconry and prebend assigned to the latter by the preceding bishop. (XIV Kalends of February.) 1155

CXLIV.—To the chapter of Novara.—Concerning a grant that is to be prohibited. (XIV Kalends of February.) 1156

CXLV.—To the bishops of Senlis and Noyon, and the abbot of Ourscamp in the diocese of Noyon.—That they not permit delegates appointed by apostolic letters to hear certain cases to promulgate new constitutions by which the king’s rights may be harmed. (VIII Kalends of February.) 1157

CXLVI.—To the archbishop and dean of Bordeaux.—He orders them to have a prebend in the church of Saintes assigned to C. … Natali, notwithstanding the appeal of the dean and chapter. (VIII Kalends of February.) 1158

CXLVII.—To the bishop of Ely and the dean and cantor of Lincoln.—Concerning the intention of the bishop of Durham to cross the sea to the Holy Land. 1160

CXLVIII.—To the bishop of Veroli.—Grant of the church of St Vincent to the monks of Casamari. (II Nones of February.) 1161

CXLIX.—To the bishops of Beauvais and Noyon, and the cantor of Reims.—He orders them to maintain B., a cleric, in possession of the church of Sarcum, granted to him by the dean of Piceio. (VII Ides of February.) 1161

CL.—To the abbots of La Couronne and Le Bornet, in the diocese of Angoulême.—He orders them to proceed without delay in the case of Peter Arlagras, a cleric to whom a prebend in the church of Périgueux was to be assigned under the command of Pope C. …. (XI Kalends of February.) 1162

CLI.—To the dean and chapter of Belin.—Concerning the reception as canon of B., provost of Beliniac. (II Kalends of February.) 1163

CLII.—To N., abbot of St John of Angély; … abbot of St Léger; and … provost of St Léger, in the diocese of Saintes. [Col. 1232]—Concerning abuse in the granting of prebends by the monks and canons of the church of St Mary Major at Poitiers. (VII Kalends of February.) 1165

CLIII.—To the prior of St Fridianus and Master B. …, canon of Pisa.—Concerning the procedure for denunciation, exception, and accusation. (I Ides of February.) 1166

CLIV.—To N., bishop of Bisignano, and the bishop-elect of Cosenza.—Concerning the abbey of St Mary of the Wood. (II Ides of February.) 1167

CLV.—To the archbishop of Salzburg and his suffragans, and others.—Against the murderers of the bishop of Würzburg. (X Kalends of February.) 1167

CLVI.—To the abbot of St Edmund of Lincoln, the dean, and P. of Blois, archdeacon of Bath.—He entrusts to them the examination of the case of G. of Perthico, archdeacon of Northumbria. (XV Kalends of March.) 1170

CLVII.—To the archbishop of Sens.—Concerning the metropolitan’s right to absolve before or after an appeal. (XIII Kalends of March.) 1171

CLVIII.—To John, priest-cardinal of the title of St Stephen on the Caelian Hill, legate of the Apostolic See.—He abolishes the abuse in Ireland whereby sons succeeded fathers and grandsons grandfathers in benefices. 1172

CLIX.—To the bishop of Castello, and the priors of Camaldoli and St Fridianus.—Concerning the reform of monasteries throughout Tuscany. (XV Kalends of March.) 1173

CLX.—To the king of England.—That he not impede ecclesiastical liberty. (X Kalends of March.) 1175

CLXI.—To the army of crusaders.—Concerning the capture of Zara. 1178

CLXII.—To the counts, barons, and other crusaders.—On the same subject. 1179
## Appendix to Book Five

CLXIII.—To the beloved sons Matthew, abbot, and the brethren of St. Lawrence of Aversa, both present and those to be regularly appointed in the future, in perpetuity. (The Ides of July.) 1181

CLXIV.—To Roger, abbot of the monastery of Saints Peter and Paul of Canterbury.—Concerning the confirmation of privileges. (The second day before the Nones of November.) 1185

## Various Documents

Letter of the abbot and convent of St. Geneviève of Paris, made between them and the bishop of Paris, concerning the parochial right of St. Geneviève and concerning the procurations due to the bishop from the church of St. Geneviève in the city and from the other churches of the aforesaid St. Geneviève. 1185

Letter of the archdeacons of Paris on the same matter. 1187

Letter of Odo, bishop of Paris, concerning the presentation made by the abbot of St. Geneviève, for the purpose of presenting Theobald, canon of St. Geneviève, to the bishop of Paris; and concerning the oath made by the said Theobald to the aforesaid bishop. 1187

Letter of G., abbot of St. Benedict of Fleury and cantor of Chartres, and J., master of the schools of Orléans, judges appointed by the lord pope concerning a certain judgment rendered by them between the bishop of Paris and the abbot of St. Geneviève of Paris. 1188

Letter containing the form of peace and settlement between Lord Odo, bishop of Paris, and the abbot and church of St. Geneviève. 1189

Letter of Elias, abbot of St. Columba of Sens, and John, master of the schools of Orléans, commissioners of the Apostolic See, concerning the confirmation of the aforesaid settlement and peace. 1190

Letter containing the form of settlement and peace between Lord Odo, bishop, and the Church of Paris on the one side, and John, abbot, and the Church of St. Geneviève on the other. 1191

Letter of Innocent III to the bishop of Paris, the abbot, and the chapter of St. Geneviève.—He confirms the settlement between them. 1191

Letter of Innocent III to the archbishops and bishops established throughout the kingdom of France.—Concerning the legitimization of the children of Philip, king of the Franks. 1193

Letters of the Gallican bishops to clergy and laity throughout the kingdom of France.—On the same subject. 1194
